class.name: NetwMultiplayer
class.brief_description: The [MultiplayerAPI] implementation for a Networked session.
class.description:
Use [method Netw.of] to get the session for a node. Most game code should use [Netw] and the handle classes instead of calling this class directly. [codeblock] var api := Netw.of(self) api.entity_despawn(route) api.scene_admit(scene, participant) [/codeblock] Method prefixes identify their subsystem and related API class: - [code]scene_*[/code]: [NetwSceneHandle] - [code]interest_*[/code]: [NetwInterestHandle] - [code]session_*[/code]: [NetwSessionHandle] - [code]clock_*[/code]: [NetwClockHandle] - [code]predict_*[/code]: [NetwPredictionHandle] - [code]entity_*[/code], [code]liveness_*[/code], and [code]spawn_*[/code]: [NetwEntity] - [code]table_*[/code]: [NetwRecordTable] - [code]schema_*[/code]: [NetwSchema] - [code]lagcomp_*[/code]: [NetwAction] - [code]peer_*[/code]: [NetwParticipant] - [code]display_*[/code]: [NetwDisplayHandle] - [code]endpoint_*[/code] and [code]embed_*[/code]: [NetwConnectHandle] - [code]transport_*[/code]: [NetwTransport] - [code]rpc_*[/code] and [code]sync_*[/code]: [NetwMemberConfig] - [code]property_set_*[/code]: [NetwPropertySet] - [code]service_*[/code]: [NetwService] - [code]persist_*[/code]: [NetwDatabase] - [code]auth_*[/code]: [NetwAuthFlow] - [code]stats_*[/code] and [code]attribution_*[/code]: [NetwPredictStats] Methods beginning with an underscore are virtual extension points. Override one in a [Script] and call its corresponding [code]_default[/code] method to use the default implementation. [codeblock] extends NetwMultiplayer
func _predict_consume(depth: int, buffer: int) -> int: if depth > 8: return NetwPredict.CONSUME_ACTION_REPLAY return predict_consume_default(depth, buffer) [/codeblock] Install the subclass with [member MultiplayerTree.api_script]. Call [code]_default[/code] directly instead of using [code]super[/code].

method.name: _display_write
method.description: Writes one display [param track] for [param entity]. With no override this returns [method display_write_default]. An override that wants the stock write calls the default method directly. A bound native method is not a virtual super call for a script subclass.

method.name: _persist_tick
method.description: Advances the persistence snapshot loop by [param delta] seconds. With no override this returns [method persist_tick_default]. [method MultiplayerAPI.poll] reaches persistence through this stage with the wall-clock gap since the last poll, so a session saves on its own cadence with no frame behind it. Override it to observe or replace that cadence, and call [method persist_tick_default] for the stock pass.

method.name: _predict_admit_frame
method.description: The override point for the prediction admission gate. With no override this returns [method predict_admit_frame_default].

method.name: _predict_consume
method.description: The override point for what authority does with a command queue that is [param depth] transitions deep against a [param buffer] it was asked to hold. With no override this returns [method predict_consume_default]. The result is a [enum NetwPredict.ConsumeAction], which replays a queued transition, holds the queue where it is, or runs dry on the last one. It is asked once per authority tick per predicted entity, so it decides pacing rather than content, and it may not read or write entity state.

method.name: _predict_drive
method.description: The override point for which input a predicted entity advances on this frame. With no override this returns [method predict_drive_default]. [param latest_input_tick] is the newest input the entity holds and [param last_driven_input_tick] is the one it last advanced on, so the two together say whether this frame has fresh input or repeats. [param frame_tick] is the label to fall back to when the entity holds no input at all. Returning [code]null[/code] is not a way to abstain. The result is rejected, a [constant EVENT_SEAM_MISUSE] is emitted, and the default's fold stands.

method.name: _predict_evaluate
method.description: The override point for the judgement that decides whether a predicted state matched the one authority reached. With no override this returns [method predict_evaluate_default]. [param domain] says whether the transition was in the predicted domain at all, [param verdict] carries any exact comparison already made, and [param field_sink] is where the per-field differences land. Returning [code]null[/code] is not a way to abstain. The result is rejected, a [constant EVENT_SEAM_MISUSE] is emitted, and the default's judgement stands, so an override with nothing to say about a case returns the default's return a result for it.

method.name: _predict_recover
method.description: The override point for the plan that says how a diverged entity is brought back onto authority's state. With no override this returns [method predict_recover_default]. [param policy] and [param correction] are what the declaration asked for, [param projection] and [param current] are the two states being reconciled, and [param tick_delta] is the step the plan is measured against. Returning [code]null[/code] is not a way to abstain. The result is rejected, a [constant EVENT_SEAM_MISUSE] is emitted, and the default's plan stands, so an override that handles one policy returns the default's return a result for the others. Withholding fields is an in-domain refinement, and the default plan does not attempt it otherwise. A divergence outside the declared domain, or one nobody could charge while a contact was still disturbing the bodies, gives no ground for deciding which fields are safe to leave predicted, so the default re-bases the whole closure instead.

method.name: _spawn_admit_frame
method.description: The override point for the spawn admission gate. With no override this returns [method spawn_admit_frame_default].

method.name: _spawn_construct
method.description: Builds the local [Node] for one entity the server told this peer to spawn. With no override this returns [method spawn_construct_default]. This is where a spawn recipe becomes a node again on a receiving peer. It constructs and returns the node without adding it to the tree, because the session owns the parenting. Returning [code]null[/code] is reported rather than treated as an empty entity. Override to pool nodes, pick a variant scene, or substitute a proxy for an entity this peer does not need in full, and call the default method directly for the node the pump would have built.

method.name: _spawn_declare
method.description: Declares that [param entity] may be materialized on other peers. With no override this returns [method spawn_declare_default]. Declaring makes an entity eligible for spawning and does not spawn it. Which peers actually receive it is an interest decision, and the session acts on that decision itself. [param recipe] is the value-only description a remote peer needs in order to construct the entity, and never carries a [Node] or an object reference, because a spawn plan has to survive serialization. Override to validate or enrich the recipe, then call the default method directly. A bound native method is not a virtual super call for a script subclass.

method.name: _spawn_undeclare
method.description: Makes [param entity] ineligible for spawning again. The default result does nothing, because the session has already recorded the withdrawal and this exists to be watched. Withdrawing stops future spawns and does not despawn the copies peers already hold. Those leave through the [enum LeavePolicy] of the layer that showed them. This is the twin of [method _spawn_declare].

method.name: _sync_admit_frame
method.description: The override point for the sync admission gate. With no override this returns [method sync_admit_frame_default].

method.name: _sync_apply_set
method.description: Writes one decoded property set into [param entity]'s component [param comp]. With no override this returns [method sync_apply_set_default]. An override that wants the stock write calls the default method directly. A bound native method is not a virtual super call for a script subclass.

method.name: _sync_decode
method.description: Applies one admitted sync body to [param entity]'s [param comp] address. Decoding runs after the sync gate validates the route and payload. It may still reject bytes that do not match the attached property set. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the payload was applied to the component ┖╴ERR_UNCONFIGURED no decoder is installed for this address [/codeblock] [param flags] carries the frame's sync bits and [param tick] the authoring tick, which is what lets a late frame be recognized as stale. [param payload] is the body [method _sync_encode] produced on the sender. With no override, this returns the decoder the running decode stage installed, and [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNCONFIGURED] outside a decode stage. The exact inverse of [method _sync_encode]. Whatever that writes, this must read, so the two are replaced together in practice even though nothing requires it.

method.name: _sync_encode
method.description: Produces the sync body one [param peer] receives for one [param tick]. Encoding is per recipient because interest already decided that peers see different worlds. The bytes returned here are the frame body only, and the carrier adds the frame envelope around them. An empty [PackedByteArray] means "nothing to send this peer this tick", which is the ordinary result for a peer whose visible entities are all unchanged. It is not an error. With no override, this returns the stock body the running encode stage armed, and an empty [PackedByteArray] outside an encode stage. The exact inverse of [method _sync_decode].

method.name: _sync_gather_set
method.description: Gathers one property set from [param entity]'s component [param comp]. With no override this returns [method sync_gather_set_default]. An override that wants the stock gather calls the default method directly. A bound native method is not a virtual super call for a script subclass.

method.name: _sync_note_ack
method.description: Records that [param peer] acknowledged everything through [param sequence]. With no override this returns [method sync_note_ack_default]. Delta encoding is only sound against a baseline the recipient is known to hold, and this is how that baseline advances. A peer whose acks stop moving keeps its old baseline, so its deltas grow rather than going wrong. [param sequence] is monotonic per peer, and an out-of-order or repeated acknowledgement is ignored rather than rewinding the baseline. An override that wants the baseline to keep advancing calls the default method directly. A bound native method is not a virtual super call for a script subclass.

method.name: _sync_note_sent
method.description: Records that [param sequence] was sent to [param peer]. With no override this returns [method sync_note_sent_default]. The send side commits its pending masked state at the moment it goes out rather than when it is acknowledged, so the delta this frame produced is the delta the next one builds on. The send-side twin of [method _sync_note_ack]. An override that wants the stock commit calls the default method directly. A bound native method is not a virtual super call for a script subclass.

method.name: _table_admit_frame
method.description: The override point for the table admission gate. With no override this returns [method table_admit_frame_default].

method.name: attribution_is_armed
method.description: Whether the grain behind [method attribution_set_armed] is being recorded.

method.name: attribution_set_armed
method.description: Arms the per-column byte table that a row frame writes as it encodes, which is the fine grain of [method attribution_snapshot]. The per-peer, per-channel and per-route byte tables are always recorded and are unaffected by this, because they cost one add per frame. Column grain costs one add per masked column per frame, which is why it is asked for rather than assumed. This is a runtime switch and not a build flavour, so a shipped game can arm it against a session that is already misbehaving.

method.name: attribution_snapshot
method.description: Where this session's bytes went, at tooling cadence. [codeblock lang=text] Dictionary ┠╴bytes_out Dictionary peer -> channel -> bytes sent ┠╴bytes_in Dictionary peer -> channel -> bytes received ┠╴route_bytes_out Dictionary route -> bytes sent ┠╴route_bytes_in Dictionary route -> bytes received ┠╴attributed_out int the sum of bytes_out ┠╴attributed_in int the sum of bytes_in ┠╴framing_out int counted as sent, carrying no frame ┠╴frames_out int frames sent ┠╴frames_in int frames received ┠╴staged_dropped_out int frames encoded and never sent ┠╴frames_in_by_channel Dictionary peer -> channel -> frames received ┠╴refused_in int frames rejected on arrival ┠╴refusals Dictionary peer -> channel -> rejection name -> count ┠╴armed bool whether column grain is being recorded ┠╴columns Dictionary a packed key -> schema, column, bits ┖╴residual Dictionary datagram and wire totals, see below [/codeblock] Every byte [method stats_snapshot] reports under [code]sent_bytes[/code] is either attributed to one peer and one channel here or reported under [code]framing_out[/code], which is the standalone acknowledgement traffic carrying no frame at all. A frame encoded and then never sent is reported under [code]staged_dropped_out[/code] and was never part of [code]sent_bytes[/code]. Route [code]0[/code] is session-scope traffic that names no entity. A send site that knows its subject while addressing no route reports it anyway, so a spawn frame is attributed to the entity it spawns. The inbound side counts frame payloads, so [code]attributed_in[/code] sits below [code]received_bytes[/code] by the envelope and datagram framing the sender spent to carry them.

method.name: auth_seat_host_identity
method.description: Stores the identity the seated flow claims for the local host against the server peer. Godot never runs the authentication callback for the host, so a listen server would otherwise be the one participant with no verified identity. The peer is not completed here. The host was never in the pending queue, and completing it would corrupt the authentication state of the peers that are. [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: auth_set_app_tag
method.description: Sets the local game-build tag stamped on every hello this session sends and required of every hello it reads. Zero disables the build gate, so a session that never sets one admits any build.

method.name: auth_set_flow
method.description: Overrides [method Netw.configure_auth] for this session. Pass [code]null[/code] to restore the project auth flow. The next peer uses the new flow.

method.name: clear
method.description: Clears the wrapped [member inner] [SceneMultiplayer]'s replication state. It does not touch this session's roster, services or entities, which [method clear_roster] and [method service_clear] own.

method.name: clear_roster
method.description: Drops everything this session holds about who is in it. That is every peer's bucket, identity and accepted [ResolvedJoin], and every participant row, clearing [member local_participant] with them. The transport is untouched, so this empties the roster of a session that is going down rather than disconnecting anyone. [method peer_forget] is the same clearing for one peer.

method.name: clock_auto_configure_offset
method.description: Opens a five-second measurement of the display offset this link actually needs, and applies the largest recommendation it saw when the window closes. It moves the live [constant CLOCK_PARAM_DISPLAY_OFFSET] and never reopens the draft that configured the clock, so the value it finds is not saved anywhere. Restarting it before the window closes replaces the measurement in progress, and a disconnect cancels it. A host measures nothing and returns immediately, because it has no link to the server to measure. So does a session whose clock was never configured.

method.name: clock_get_config
method.description: The clock this session is running right now, rebuilt on every call, so a value changed since through [method clock_set_param] reads back here as well as through [method clock_get_param]. Returns a copy of the active clock configuration. The session does not retain the original [NetwClockConfig], and modifying the returned copy has no effect.

method.name: clock_get_display_tick
method.description: The tick a visual should render, which is [method clock_get_tick] less [constant CLOCK_PARAM_DISPLAY_OFFSET] and never below zero. The gap between the two is the buffer that smoothing spends.

method.name: clock_get_monitor
method.description: One diagnostic clock counter as a [float]. The vocabulary is [enum ClockMonitor], and every member of it is a uniform scalar so a caller never has to know which key of which dictionary carries it. The five cadence monitors, [constant CLOCK_MONITOR_PHYSICS_FRAMES] through [constant CLOCK_MONITOR_POLL_HZ], count what the engine actually delivered rather than what was asked of it. That is how a starved host is told apart from a mistuned one.

method.name: clock_get_param
method.description: The current value of one tunable clock knob. The vocabulary is [enum ClockParam], and the return type follows the knob. A count returns an [int], a duration or a factor returns a [float], and a switch returns a [bool].

method.name: clock_get_physics_steps_per_tick
method.description: [constant CLOCK_MONITOR_PHYSICS_FACTOR] as a whole number, never below one. The physics server runs exactly one step per frame, so a tick can be worth one step or two but never one and a fifth. A fractional factor is a declaration the engine cannot honour, and the gate's step budget rounds it here rather than pretending otherwise.

method.name: clock_get_simulation_behind_count
method.description: How many frames wanted a tick the gate's ceiling rejected. A gated clock announces one tick per frame at most, so a peer whose physics cannot sustain [constant CLOCK_PARAM_TICKRATE] times [method clock_get_physics_steps_per_tick] steps per wall second cannot catch up by doubling a frame. Sustained growth here means this peer is too slow to predict, which no netcode setting repairs.

method.name: clock_get_tick
method.description: The current server-calibrated simulation tick.

method.name: clock_ingest_pong
method.description: Feeds one round-trip sample into the calibration and returns the drift metrics that sample produced. Calibration keeps the schedule aligned with a server's without ever teleporting the playhead. [constant SYNC_MODE_SNAP] takes the whole correction at once. [constant SYNC_MODE_STRETCH] takes a fraction of it per frame, falling back to a snap once the divergence passes [constant CLOCK_PARAM_PANIC_SNAP_THRESHOLD], which is a real desync rather than drift. The target is a continuous clock position rather than a whole tick, and that is deliberate. Rounding the [param server_tick_phase] away would make the target jump by a full tick as a ping's arrival phase slid across a server boundary, and [constant SYNC_MODE_STRETCH] would then chase that sawtooth for about a second at a time, dragging the local tick boundary back and forth through the server's. The margin that used to ride on that rounding is [constant CLOCK_PARAM_LEAD_TICKS], which is explicit. The returned [Dictionary] is the same shape [signal clock_pong_received] carries as [code]data[/code]. [codeblock lang=text] Dictionary ┠╴rtt_raw float this sample's round trip, in seconds ┠╴rtt_avg float the running average round trip ┠╴rtt_jitter float the running jitter estimate ┠╴diff int ticks the calibration moved this peer ┠╴tick int the tick after calibrating ┠╴display_offset float the offset the display is running ┠╴recommended_display_offset float the offset this sample recommends ┠╴is_stable bool whether jitter is under threshold ┖╴is_synchronized bool whether a calibration has ever landed [/codeblock]

method.name: clock_is_configured
method.description: Whether a configurator has registered its [NetwClockConfig]. An unconfigured clock is inert rather than absent. The tick stays where it was placed, so a session with no clock reads a tick that never moves.

method.name: clock_is_gated
method.description: Whether any gate armed by [method clock_set_gate] is still held.

method.name: clock_is_simulating
method.description: Whether this frame's simulated world may advance. Stays [code]true[/code] for a whole session unless a gate is armed, so a game that predicts nothing never sees a held frame.

method.name: clock_is_stable
method.description: Whether [constant CLOCK_MONITOR_RTT_JITTER] is below [constant CLOCK_PARAM_JITTER_STABILITY_THRESHOLD].

method.name: clock_is_synchronized
method.description: Whether a calibration has landed. The first [method clock_ingest_pong] sets it and hard-aligns, so [constant SYNC_MODE_STRETCH] begins already converged.

method.name: clock_physics_step
method.description: Pays [param delta] seconds of frame time into the tick schedule and announces whatever whole ticks it buys. The remainder is banked rather than dropped, so two half frames are worth exactly one tick and no time is invented or lost. A frame longer than [constant CLOCK_PARAM_STALL_THRESHOLD] is read as a hitch rather than as simulated time and resets the accumulator, and no frame may buy more than [constant CLOCK_PARAM_MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME]. A session that consumed a clock configuration calls this itself, once per [SceneTree] physics frame, with that frame's actual delta. A clock left at [constant CLOCK_PARAM_MANUAL_TICK] ignores that pump so a rig can own the schedule.

method.name: clock_request_handshake
method.description: Asks server authority for its tickrate over the clock's handshake channel, so the two rates can be compared before any tick is calibrated against them. The server returns its own tickrate, and a reply that disagrees is what [method clock_set_mismatch_action] decides the response to. Only a peer that is not server authority calls this. The session runs it once per transport generation, as soon as a connection to the server exists, so a host never asks itself.

method.name: clock_send_ping
method.description: Sends the local wall-clock timestamp to server authority over the clock's ping channel, unreliably, because a lost sample is cheaper than a late one. The server echoes it back with its own tick, and that reply lands as [signal clock_pong_received] once [method clock_ingest_pong] has processed it. The handshake's reply triggers the first ping, and later pings repeat on whatever schedule drives recalibration.

method.name: clock_set_gate
method.description: Arms a simulation gate when [param armed] is [code]true[/code] and releases one otherwise. Gates nest, so the world resumes on the release that matches the first arm. The physics server runs exactly one step per frame and takes no argument about how long that step is, so the only way a clock can make a tick worth the same amount of time on two peers is to decide which frames the world may step at all. A gated clock pays each announced tick into a budget of whole steps and spends one per simulated frame, and a frame with nothing to spend holds. [codeblock lang=text] clock_set_gate(true) a body the physics server integrates tick announced -> credit += clock_get_physics_steps_per_tick() frame spends -> credit -= 1, clock_is_simulating() true no credit -> clock_is_simulating() false, the world holds clock_set_gate(false) the last release restores every frame [/codeblock]

method.name: clock_set_mismatch_action
method.description: What a session does when a clock handshake reply carries a tickrate different from its own, one of the [enum MismatchAction] values. [constant MISMATCH_ACTION_WARN] is the default because a tickrate difference is a configuration mistake rather than a protocol violation, and a session that disconnects on it gives a game no way to say so.

method.name: clock_set_param
method.description: Turns one tunable clock knob, returning [constant @GlobalScope.OK]. Rejects [constant CLOCK_PARAM_TICKRATE] with [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAUTHORIZED], because a tickrate that differs between two peers means their ticks are worth different amounts of simulated time. It is settable through the [NetwClockConfig] a game declares with [method Netw.configure_clock] alone, and a peer that connects carrying a different one is reported by [signal clock_tickrate_mismatch]. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the knob was turned ┠╴ERR_UNAUTHORIZED param was CLOCK_PARAM_TICKRATE ┖╴ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER param names no known knob [/codeblock]

method.name: clock_set_synchronized
method.description: Declares whether the calibration still holds. A client that loses its server clears this so the next handshake calibrates from scratch rather than nudging a stale target.

method.name: clock_step
method.description: Advances the clock by [param count] whole ticks, announcing each one exactly as a pumped frame would. This and [method clock_physics_step] announce identically, so a stepped rig and a running session cannot mean different things by a tick. They differ in one respect. A step is not a frame, so this brackets no [signal clock_before_tick_loop], and a caller that needs the bracket opens it with [method clock_tick_loop].

method.name: clock_tick_loop
method.description: Opens the frame bracket when [param open] is [code]true[/code] and closes it otherwise, announcing [signal clock_before_tick_loop] and [signal clock_after_tick_loop]. A frame-tier entity authors, sends and consumes in that pass, so a rig that steps ticks without bracketing them leaves such an entity at drive zero however many ticks it runs.

method.name: complete_auth
method.description: Ends [param id]'s authentication handshake on [member inner], moving it out of [method get_authenticating_peers] and into the connected roster. Returns [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNCONFIGURED] when this session wraps no [member inner], and otherwise whatever the wrapped [SceneMultiplayer] returns. [method send_auth] carries the handshake's own data, and this is the call that closes it. Both keep [SceneMultiplayer]'s own spelling, so a game swapping one session for the other finds the authentication handshake under the same names.

method.name: core_of
method.description: The same session [method of] resolves, as the [NetwMultiplayer] itself rather than as the object it publishes. This is what a caller wants when it is about to call a session verb, and [method of] is what it wants when it is about to compare against an installed [MultiplayerAPI].

method.name: disconnect_peer
method.description: Closes [param id]'s connection outright, with no authority check and no notice sent first. Keeps [SceneMultiplayer]'s own spelling, so a game swapping one session for the other closes a peer the same way. [method peer_kick] is the server-authority call built on this. It rejects without [member is_host], announces [signal peer_kicked] to the peer, and only then closes it. This is the bare call underneath, for a caller that has already made those decisions itself.

method.name: display_declare
method.description: Declares [param track] on [param entity]'s component [param comp], wiring [param spec] as the interpolation the display pump applies to that property and marking the entity's display state dirty so the wiring takes effect. Returns [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST] when [param entity] is not registered, [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_INVALID_DATA] when [param track] is empty or [param spec] is [code]null[/code], and [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAVAILABLE] when [param comp] names no live node on [param entity]. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the track was declared ┠╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST entity is not registered ┠╴ERR_INVALID_DATA track is empty, or spec is null ┖╴ERR_UNAVAILABLE comp names no live node on entity [/codeblock]

method.name: display_get_param
method.description: Reads back the display setting named by [param param] for [param entity], the same [enum DisplayParam] vocabulary [method display_set_param] writes, from [constant DISPLAY_PARAM_ROLE] through [constant DISPLAY_PARAM_VISUAL_ROOT]. Returns [code]null[/code] when [param entity] has no committed display declaration.

method.name: display_get_track_stat
method.description: Reads one live display measurement for [param entity]. A stat about the whole display ignores [param track], and a stat about one channel uses it to select a declared property. [codeblock lang=text] the whole display pump_mode pumped_frames channels ambiguous role starvation_ticks display_lag one track sleeping offset_armed offset_held buffer buffer_size [/codeblock] An unknown stat or an entity with no runtime returns [code]null[/code].

method.name: display_get_value
method.description: The last value written to [param entity]'s display channel [param track], as [method display_write_default] or [method display_snap] left it. Returns [code]null[/code] when [param entity] has no live display runtime or [param track] names no declared channel.

method.name: display_reset
method.description: Clears what [param entity] displays, applies the live source values to its visual, and re-seats the playhead at the session's current display offset. A predicted display that teleports the body snaps its visual to the new truth through this, so the smoothing resumes from where the body now is rather than gliding across the correction.

method.name: display_set_callback
method.description: Replaces the [Callable] [method display_write_default] calls in place of writing [param entity]'s target node or item directly, a no-op when [param entity] is not registered. A valid [param callback] is called with [code](entity, track, value)[/code] on every default write, and an invalid one clears it. Installing a callback drops any [method display_set_target_item] item, because the two routes are exclusive.

method.name: display_set_param
method.description: Writes [param value] to the display setting named by [param param] for [param entity], covering every [enum DisplayParam] constant from [constant DISPLAY_PARAM_ROLE] through [constant DISPLAY_PARAM_VISUAL_ROOT]. [constant DISPLAY_PARAM_VISUAL_ROOT] reads its value two ways. A [NodePath] or [String] is stored as written, which is what lets a visual be named before the node exists, and any other value is read as a component id and resolved through [method display_set_target_item].

method.name: display_set_target_item
method.description: Names [param item], a [RenderingServer] canvas item or instance, as what [method display_write_default] writes [param entity]'s pose to when no node target and no [method display_set_callback] callback take precedence. An invalid [param item] clears the target. Setting an item drops any installed callback, because the two routes are exclusive.

method.name: display_snap
method.description: Forces [param entity]'s display channel [param track] to [param value] immediately, bypassing the interpolation the channel would otherwise apply. A no-op when [param entity] has no live display runtime or [param track] names no declared channel. A display that teleports rather than glides through a correction calls this so the visible pose jumps with the body instead of smoothing across the correction.

method.name: display_write_default
method.description: The stock body of [method _display_write]. It resolves the declared display [param track] for [param entity] and writes [param value] through that track's target. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the write landed, or a callback consumed it ┠╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST the track resolves to no target ┖╴ERR_INVALID_DATA value is neither a Transform2D nor a Transform3D [/codeblock]

method.name: embed_adopt_inner
method.description: Replaces [member inner] in place, rebinding every transport edge this session listens on and re-emits, and re-applying the session's auth configuration to the new transport. An embedding calls this when the [SceneMultiplayer] under a live session has to change without the session itself being torn down and rebuilt. An auth callback already set on [param inner] is adopted, and one carrying none leaves this session's callback alone.

method.name: embed_dispose
method.description: Releases the whole graph this session owns, and is the one teardown call an embedding makes. It runs once however many callers ask, returning immediately when the teardown has already begun. It first drains everything already scheduled, the way [method session_flush_deferred] does, because a session that ends has no next frame and the nodes that work was written against are still standing here. Only then does it release the scenes, the session state, the display runtimes, the replication of every property, the registered calls, the services and the roster.

method.name: embed_is_disposing
method.description: Whether this session has started a deliberate shutdown. This distinguishes local shutdown from a lost server connection. False for the whole life of a session that is still in use, and true from the first moment of teardown onward. A session never comes back from it.

method.name: embed_offer_bare_level
method.description: Records [param level] as the default single scene a scoped embedding offers, consumed by the next [method embed_settle]. The embedding captures it synchronously, so a node dropped in afterwards never becomes the candidate. A root install offers nothing and passes [code]null[/code].

method.name: embed_phase
method.description: The current bootstrap phase of this session's authoring, advanced once by the installing embedding through [method embed_settle]. Pairs with [signal embed_phase_changed]. This is a different question from [member state]. A session at [constant EMBED_PHASE_LIVE] is still [constant SESSION_STATE_OFFLINE] until it hosts or joins, because this returns how far the embedding has come and [member state] returns whether the session is connected.

method.name: embed_poll_transport
method.description: Sends and receives one batch of datagrams, then sweeps what arriving traffic retires. Returns [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNCONFIGURED] when the session holds no [member inner]. A datagram is only sent or received here, so whatever drives this call decides how often a peer's simulation can see the network. Engine polling alone drives it once per rendered frame, which makes a peer's framerate govern its neighbour's input arrival. Commands pile up and land in clumps, and a clumped arrival reaches a body as a transition that spent the wrong amount of physics rather than as latency. So the transport is also serviced once per tick of the session's clock, which is the guarantee this needs. Servicing a peer more often than once per simulated tick is harmless and only lowers latency, so the engine poll keeps its call and a session with no clock is unaffected. [codeblock lang=text] clock_before_tick_loop record the frame that closed clock_on_tick tick_step clock_after_tick flush this tick's frames, then embed_poll_transport() clock_after_tick_loop drive and consume, against a queue the tick just filled [/codeblock] Safe to call again from game code that wants the newest inbound state before it runs.

method.name: embed_settle
method.description: Resolves this session's authored declarations as one ordered step and advances [method embed_phase] to [constant EMBED_PHASE_LIVE]. Every session runs the same [constant EMBED_PHASE_DECLARING] to [constant EMBED_PHASE_LIVE] sequence, so the order declarations resolve in never depends on the order [method Node._enter_tree] happens to visit them. It is called once at the first idle frame after the session is installed. A [MultiplayerTree] defers it from [method Node._enter_tree] so the call lands after every declaration around it, and the autoload calls it on a one-shot [signal SceneTree.process_frame]. A call past [constant EMBED_PHASE_DECLARING] returns [constant @GlobalScope.OK] and resolves nothing again. It returns [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNCONFIGURED] when a channel finished with no handler registered for it, and the phase still reaches [constant EMBED_PHASE_LIVE], because an unhandled channel is worth reporting and is not a reason to hold every declaration open. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the phase reached LIVE, every channel had a handler ┖╴ERR_UNCONFIGURED the phase still reached LIVE, but a peer-scoped channel finished with no handler registered [/codeblock] [codeblock] api.embed_offer_bare_level(level) # optional default single scene api.embed_settle() # DECLARING -> SETTLING -> LIVE [/codeblock]

method.name: endpoint_add
method.description: Adds a row for [param address] on [param transport] and returns its handle, announcing [signal endpoint_added] when the row is new, invalid when [param transport] names nothing this session holds. [codeblock] var endpoint := api.endpoint_add( api.transport_find(&"ENetMultiplayerPeer"), "203.0.113.42:21253") api.session_prepare_join(&"Dev", []) api.multiplayer_peer = peer [/codeblock] A handle identifies one address and transport pair. Adding the same pair returns the existing handle without emitting a signal.

method.name: endpoint_find
method.description: The handle for the row [param transport] and [param address] name, invalid when this session holds no such row.

method.name: endpoint_get_param
method.description: One field of the row [param endpoint] names, named by [param param]. [code]null[/code] when this session holds no such row.

method.name: endpoint_get_state
method.description: What the last probe or listing returned for the row [param endpoint] names, named by [param state]. [constant ENDPOINT_STATE_STATUS] returns [constant @GlobalScope.FAILED] before anything has probed the row, which is not the same as a probe that failed.

method.name: endpoint_list
method.description: Every row this session knows how to reach as an [RID] handle, caller-added rows first and then whatever a listing published. This is what a server browser draws.

method.name: endpoint_probe
method.description: Probes the row [param endpoint] names without joining it, announcing [signal endpoint_updated] when it returns. What it found is read back through [method endpoint_get_state].

method.name: endpoint_refresh
method.description: Re-probes every endpoint and emits [signal endpoint_updated] for each result. Probes run serially.

method.name: endpoint_remove
method.description: Drops the row [param endpoint] names, announcing [signal endpoint_removed].

method.name: endpoint_set_param
method.description: Writes [param value] onto the row [param endpoint] names, announcing [signal endpoint_updated]. [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST] when no such row exists, [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER] for any [param param] but [constant ENDPOINT_PARAM_DISPLAY_NAME], which is the only field a caller may rewrite. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the row was written ┠╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST no such row exists ┖╴ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER param names anything but ENDPOINT_PARAM_DISPLAY_NAME [/codeblock]

method.name: entity_add_property_set
method.description: Attaches the sealed property [param set] to [param entity]'s [param comp] address and registers it with the sync pipeline. Only a sealed set may be attached, because sealing is what fixes membership order, and membership order is wire order. A set that could still gain a column could not be decoded by a peer that attached it earlier. [param set] is created by [method property_set_create] and sealed by [method property_set_seal]. [param comp] is the registration-time component id, [code]0[/code] for the entity root, and one set may be attached at each [param comp]. Returns [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST] when [param entity] or [param set] names nothing valid, [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_INVALID_DATA] when the set exists but was never sealed, and [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAVAILABLE] when [param comp] resolves to no live node on this entity. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the set was attached ┠╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST entity or set names nothing valid ┠╴ERR_INVALID_DATA the set exists but was never sealed ┠╴ERR_UNAVAILABLE comp resolves to no live node on this entity ┖╴ERR_UNCONFIGURED the session has no sync pipeline [/codeblock]

method.name: entity_admit
method.description: Reserves the next route and binds it to [param entity], the server-side counterpart to a client learning a route off the wire. Returns the route on success, and [code]0[/code] both off server authority and for an [param entity] [method entity_create] never created. An entity that already carries a route returns that route again rather than reserving a second one.

method.name: entity_adopt
method.description: Takes one node that is already in the scene into replication, returning its entity handle. The entity is armed where it stands rather than reconstructed, so peers that already hold the node keep it. An invalid [RID] means the pipeline declined it. The twin of [method entity_replicate], and the two are not interchangeable. This one takes a node the tree already holds and enrols it where it stands, while [method entity_replicate] rejects such a node and builds one from a scene recipe.

method.name: entity_bind_node
method.description: Attaches [param node] as the scene representation of [param entity], arming it as a [NetwEntity] and binding it to the route [param entity] already holds. Returns [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST] for a handle [method entity_create] never created, [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_INVALID_DATA] for a null [param node] or for an entity with no route yet, [constant @GlobalScope.OK] again for the same node re-bound to the same entity, and [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_ALREADY_EXISTS] when a different node already holds the binding. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the node was bound, or was already this entity's node ┠╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST entity names a handle entity_create never created ┠╴ERR_INVALID_DATA node is null, or entity has no route yet ┖╴ERR_ALREADY_EXISTS a different node already holds the binding [/codeblock]

method.name: entity_bind_route
method.description: Assigns [param route] to [param entity], the route a peer already knows the entity by rather than one this session would reserve on its own. Rejects with [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST] for an unminted [param entity], [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_INVALID_DATA] for a [param route] that is not positive, and [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_ALREADY_IN_USE] when the route is already bound to a different entity. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the route was assigned ┠╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST entity is unminted ┠╴ERR_INVALID_DATA route is not positive ┖╴ERR_ALREADY_IN_USE route is already bound to a different entity [/codeblock]

method.name: entity_call
method.description: Calls [param method] on [param entity]'s [param comp] component over the wire, addressed the way [method rpc_call] addresses anything. It goes by route to [param peer], or to every peer that may see the entity when [param peer] is zero. Each rejection has a distinct result and occurs before anything is sent. Rejected calls are not counted as dropped packets. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the call was sent ┠╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST no component node and the entity is not live, or the node has no such method at all ┠╴ERR_UNAVAILABLE the entity is live but this session resolves no node for that component yet ┖╴ERR_UNCONFIGURED the node has the method, and nothing declared it remote [/codeblock] Either a [method Netw.configure_rpc] declaration or the engine's own [code]@rpc[/code] annotation satisfies this. A node with no script can satisfy neither, because both live on a script.

method.name: entity_create
method.description: Creates a fresh entity handle and returns its [RID]. The handle carries no route, no node and no state beyond [constant ENTITY_STATE_UNKNOWN] until [method entity_bind_route] or [method entity_admit] gives it one.

method.name: entity_describe
method.description: What this session holds about [param route], as one read a watcher can put beside an event record. [code]stage[/code] carries a [enum NetwEntity.Stage] value and [code]liveness[/code] carries an [enum EntityState] value. [codeblock lang=text] Dictionary ┠╴route int the route asked about ┠╴entity_id StringName the durable label ┠╴peer_id int the peer this entity represents, 0 for a server-owned one ┠╴stage int the entity's Stage ┠╴controller int the peer that steers it, 0 for the server ┠╴liveness int the entity's EntityState ┖╴layers Array the interest layers it belongs to, in join order [/codeblock] Empty for a route this session holds no record for. A lifecycle event names its subject and not its state, because attaching a projection to every event costs every session that emits one. This is the read that returns the state, and [constant EVENT_DESPAWNED] carries the last one instead, since a route outlives its entity by exactly one event.

method.name: entity_despawn
method.description: Ends [param entity] on every peer that holds it, returning [constant @GlobalScope.OK] when the tear-down was accepted. This ends the entity rather than hiding it. The route is retired and never reissued, so a receiver drops its row instead of expecting the entity back. To stop one peer seeing an entity that is still alive, use [method interest_leave], which can be undone. Rejected with [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAUTHORIZED] off server authority, because a client that could end another peer's entity could end any of them. [param opts] carries the linger window, the save flush and the deferred-free choice for this one call. It is the options of a call rather than an authored policy, which is what [NetwDespawnConfig] is. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the tear-down was accepted ┠╴ERR_UNAUTHORIZED called off server authority ┖╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST entity resolves to no view [/codeblock] [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: entity_from_route
method.description: The entity handle bound to [param route], or a null [RID] when no live entity holds that route. The inverse of [method entity_get_route].

method.name: entity_get_epoch
method.description: The epoch [param entity]'s route is currently on, which advances each time the same route is reissued to a new identity after a tombstone. A route not yet issued returns its epoch as it stands before any admission.

method.name: entity_get_node
method.description: The [Node] bound to [param entity] through [method entity_bind_node], or [code]null[/code] for a handle with no scene representation.

method.name: entity_get_parent
method.description: The entity handle for [param entity]'s parent entity, or a null [RID] when [param entity] has no bound node, no parent entity, or a parent whose node has since left the scene.

method.name: entity_get_peer
method.description: The peer id [param entity]'s bound node names as its controller, or [code]0[/code] for a handle with no bound node.

method.name: entity_get_route
method.description: The route [param entity] is bound to, or [code]0[/code] when it has none yet. This is the address [method entity_call] and the sync and spawn channels use to reach the entity over the wire.

method.name: entity_get_state
method.description: Where [param entity]'s route sits on the [enum EntityState] ladder, as this peer currently knows it. A handle with no route returns [constant ENTITY_STATE_UNKNOWN].

method.name: entity_get_view
method.description: The live wrapper carrying [param entity], or [code]null[/code]. A wrapper a death retired is not live and returns [code]null[/code] here, for the rest of the cycle in which it was retired.

method.name: entity_grant_control
method.description: Hands control of [param entity] to [param peer]. A no-op off server authority or for a handle with no bound node.

method.name: entity_of
method.description: The entity handle [param node] stands for, adopting the record on the way. It is an adopt over the record at or above [param node], which is one verb rather than two because every caller wanted both halves, and a caller that took only the first would hold a handle the index does not.

method.name: entity_replicate
method.description: Arms [param node] for replicated construction and returns its entity handle. An invalid [RID] means the pipeline declined the node, which is the same result a session with no pipeline installed gives. [param node] must not be inside the tree yet. Its identity is taken before it enters, so a receiver rebuilding it from the scene recipe agrees about which entity arrived. [method entity_adopt] is the call for a node already mounted.

method.name: event_arm
method.description: Widens event capture to every value of [enum Event] when [param enabled] is [code]true[/code], and narrows it back to only what an installed [method event_watch] names when [code]false[/code]. While disarmed, an event no watch names is neither recorded nor delivered, so a session nobody is observing pays nothing for this. Arming is what lets [method event_ring] return a result for a route no watch was installed on.

method.name: event_ring
method.description: Drains and returns everything the session recorded on [param route], oldest first, as event records shaped exactly as [method event_watch] documents. Route [code]0[/code] is the session's own history, since a ring is kept per route. Reading drains. The ring is emptied by the call, so a second read returns nothing the first already took, and an observer that must not lose a row reads this on a schedule of its own. A record is created only for a row that is drained, so a ring nobody reads costs nothing but the row. Each drained row is a copy, so writing one reaches neither the ring nor another reader.

method.name: event_unwatch
method.description: Removes the watch [method event_watch] returned [param id] for, returning [code]true[/code] when a watch was there to remove and [code]false[/code] otherwise. An event that watch alone kept armed stops being recorded once no other watch names it and [method event_arm] does not hold it open.

method.name: event_watch
method.description:
Installs a watch for every value of [enum Event] in [param events] and returns its id, which [method event_unwatch] takes back. [param sink] is called once per matching act with one record. [codeblock] var id := api.event_watch( [NetwMultiplayer.EVENT_DESPAWNED], {route = car_route}, {}, _on_despawn)
func _on_despawn(record: Dictionary) -> void: print(record.tick, " ", record.verdict) [/codeblock] [param target] narrows by subject and [param predicate] by content. [param opts] carries [code]once[/code], [code]dedupe[/code], [code]phase[/code] and a [code]note[/code]. [codeblock lang=text] Dictionary ┠╴route int only acts about this entity ┠╴entity_id StringName the same, named before a route exists ┖╴peer int only acts involving this peer [/codeblock] Every record carries every key below, so a sink reads by key and never checks for one. [codeblock lang=text] Dictionary ┠╴event int which act, one value of Event ┠╴event_name String that value's name, empty when it has none ┠╴phase int 0 before the act, 1 after it ┠╴tick int the session tick the act was raised at ┠╴route int the subject, 0 when no entity is one ┠╴entity_id StringName the subject's identity, empty if unknown ┠╴peer int the peer involved, 0 when none is ┠╴verdict int the Error returned, OK when not a verdict ┠╴detail Dictionary what this decision read, keys per event ┖╴model Dictionary the subject's last state, see below [/codeblock] A later version may add a key, so a sink that rejects an unknown one breaks on an addition that costs it nothing. [code]detail[/code] holds what the decision read. A gate carries [code]{sender, channel, comp, tick, size}[/code] and a verdict adds [code]{stage, reason}[/code]. It never carries payload bytes and never a [Node], whose lifetime would outlive the record. [code]model[/code] is filled only on an event that ends its subject, with the last state recorded while that subject existed, so the worst stop in the system has the whole final state in hand. Every other event leaves it empty, because its subject is alive and one named read away. [code]entity_id[/code] is filled from the last identity seen on the route, so a watch naming an entity by id still matches the one event that ends its life, which knows only the route. A sink is called for its effect and its return value is discarded. Which watches see one act is decided before the first sink runs, so installing or withdrawing a watch inside a sink changes the next act and never the one it is handling. [code]detail[/code] and [code]model[/code] are each sink's own copy. An act raised off the main thread is delivered after the fact, because a sink runs on the main thread only.

method.name: event_watches
method.description: Every watch this session holds, one row each, carrying the watch's id, the events it asked for, its target and predicate, its options and its hit count. [method event_watch] is what installs one.

method.name: get_authenticating_peers
method.description: The ids of every peer whose connection has completed the transport handshake but not yet finished authentication. Returns an empty array before a [MultiplayerPeer] is installed.

method.name: interest_admits
method.description: Whether [param entity] is currently visible to [param peer], read from the committed interest matrix [method interest_flush_now] last folded. Returns [code]false[/code] when [param peer] is not a live registered peer or [param entity] is not registered, rather than treating either as admitted by default.

method.name: interest_entity_has_filter
method.description: Whether [param entity] is subject to interest filtering at all, rather than being open to every peer by default. On the server this reads whether [param entity] belongs to any committed layer. Off the server it reads whether the local [member NetwEntity.interest] declaration names any label. An entity that returns [code]false[/code] here needs no [method interest_wire_admits] check, because nothing has ever narrowed who receives it.

method.name: interest_explain
method.description: A short, stable string naming why [param entity] is or is not visible to [param peer], read by walking the same admission chain [method interest_admits] tests. Returns [code]"peer is not registered"[/code] or [code]"entity is not registered"[/code] when either identity does not resolve, one of the intent- or layer-denial reasons naming the route that stopped it, or [code]"admitted"[/code] when nothing denies it. This is a diagnostic string for logging and tests, not a stable API contract to branch on.

method.name: interest_flush_now
method.description: Folds every staged driver mutation into the committed interest matrix at once, in the caller's frame, rather than waiting for the settle a cascade of admissions, releases and layer mutations coalesces under. The committed matrix is what [method interest_admits], [method interest_get_row] and every send verdict read, so a layer edge written and not yet flushed is a mutation nothing can observe. This is the verb that makes it observable now. [codeblock] layer.add_viewer(peer) api.interest_flush_now() assert(api.interest_admits(entity, peer)) [/codeblock] A layer driver installed through [method interest_layer_set_driver_callback] can reject the fold. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the matrix committed ┠╴ERR_INVALID_DATA a driver returned something other than an Array ┖╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST a driver named an entity this session does not hold [/codeblock]

method.name: interest_get_membership
method.description: The interest layers [param entity] currently belongs to, as [RID] handles opened on demand for any committed layer that has none open yet. Reading this never changes what [param entity] is admitted to, only which layers already have a live [NetwInterestLayer] view.

method.name: interest_get_row
method.description: The committed admission row for [param entity], a bitset with one bit per live peer sized to the peer table [method interest_flush_now] last committed. [method interest_admits] tests one bit of exactly this row. Returns an empty array when [param entity] is not registered.

method.name: interest_is_filtered
method.description: Whether [param entity] is subject to a visibility filter at all, which is what lets a send skip the per-peer verdict for an entity nothing narrows. On server authority the result is the committed row, so an entity no layer names is unfiltered however it was declared. Off the server the committed row is empty until the server admits the entity, so the result is the entity's own declared labels, read from the interest facet's declaration.

method.name: interest_join
method.description: Adds [param entity] to the declaration for [param layer_id]. If [param entity] is live on server authority, the layer's live membership changes in the same call. The declaration is stored on the entity record, so authoring performed before session attachment survives packing, tree exits, and re-entry.

method.name: interest_layer
method.description: Returns the [NetwInterestLayer] addressed by [param name], opening it in the session's interest engine on first use. A second call with the same [param name] returns a handle to the same layer, so declaring a layer twice never splits its membership.

method.name: interest_layer_add_entity
method.description: Puts [param entity] into [param layer], so every viewer of that layer becomes a peer this entity is sent to. The write is staged rather than applied. It lands at the next interest flush, which is what lets a run of membership changes settle together. [method interest_flush_now] forces it in the caller's own frame. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the entity was staged into the layer ┠╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST layer or entity names nothing valid ┠╴ERR_UNAUTHORIZED called off server authority ┖╴ERR_UNAVAILABLE the layer rejected the entity [/codeblock]

method.name: interest_layer_add_viewer
method.description: Makes [param peer] a viewer of [param layer], so it is sent every entity the layer holds. Viewing and membership are the two halves of a layer and neither implies the other. A peer can view a layer it has no entity in, and an entity can sit in a layer nobody views. The write is staged, as it is for [method interest_layer_add_entity]. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the peer was staged as a viewer ┠╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST layer names nothing valid ┖╴ERR_INVALID_DATA peer is 0 [/codeblock]

method.name: interest_layer_create
method.description: Opens the layer called [param name] and returns its handle, creating it when no layer holds that name yet. Create-on-demand is the difference between this and [method interest_layer_find], which only looks. Asking twice for one name returns the same handle, so a caller that cannot know whether it is first does not have to check.

method.name: interest_layer_find
method.description: The handle of the layer called [param name], or an invalid [RID] when no layer holds that name. This only looks. [method interest_layer_create] is the half that opens one, and keeping the two apart is what lets a caller ask whether a layer exists without bringing it into being by asking.

method.name: interest_layer_free
method.description: Drops [param layer] and everything it held, which is its viewers, its entities, its params and its callbacks. An entity in no surviving layer stops being sent to anyone who only saw it through this one. Freeing a handle that names no layer is not an error.

method.name: interest_layer_ids
method.description: Returns a copy of the layer labels declared for [param entity]. Clearing the returned array does not change the declaration.

method.name: interest_layer_named
method.description: Returns the [NetwInterestLayer] already open under [param name], or a null reference if nothing has opened it yet. Unlike [method interest_layer] this never creates one, so it is the read a caller reaches for when opening a layer as a side effect would be wrong.

method.name: interest_layer_remove_viewer
method.description: Stops [param peer] viewing [param layer]. A peer that was not a viewer is not an error. Whether the peer stops seeing an entity depends on the rest of its membership. An entity it still reaches through another layer keeps arriving. What happens to the entities it no longer sees is the layer's [enum LeavePolicy], set through [method interest_layer_set_param].

method.name: interest_layer_set_driver_callback
method.description: Installs [param callback] as the driver that decides [param layer]'s membership, replacing whatever hand-written membership the layer held. A driver runs once per interest flush and returns the whole membership for that pass, which is what makes a rule-based layer (everything within a radius, everything in a room) one function rather than a stream of add and remove calls. Passing an invalid [Callable] removes the driver and returns the layer to hand-written membership.

method.name: interest_layer_set_monitor_callback
method.description: Installs [param callback] as [param layer]'s observer, called as entities and viewers enter and leave it. This watches and does not decide. It cannot change membership, which is what [method interest_layer_set_driver_callback] installs, and a watcher that changed the layer it watches would feed itself. The callback is dropped when [method interest_layer_free] frees the layer, so it never outlives what it watches.

method.name: interest_layer_set_param
method.description: Writes one authored setting on [param layer], selected by [param param] from [enum LayerParam]. These are the layer's rules rather than its contents. They say what happens to the entities a departing viewer stops seeing, and whether those entities keep being drawn. [method interest_layer_add_entity] and [method interest_layer_add_viewer] are the contents.

method.name: interest_layer_view
method.description: A read-only [NetwInterestLayer] over [param layer], or [code]null[/code] when the handle names no layer. It is a view rather than a copy. It reads the live layer, so a caller holding one sees membership as it changes rather than as it stood when the view was taken.

method.name: interest_layers
method.description: Returns every [NetwInterestLayer] this session currently holds open, in no particular order. A layer cleared from the interest engine still appears here until [method interest_layer_free] releases its handle.

method.name: interest_leave
method.description: Removes [param entity] from the declaration for [param layer_id]. If [param entity] is live on server authority, the layer's live membership changes in the same call.

method.name: interest_monitor_snapshot
method.description: How many layers, entities and viewers there are, and how much they are changing, across every [NetwInterestLayer] this session holds. [codeblock lang=text] Dictionary ┠╴layers int declared layer count ┠╴entities_filtered int entities carrying membership ┠╴visible_edges int admitted (entity, peer) pairs ┠╴dirty_entities int entities awaiting the next flush ┠╴relay_backlog int pending liveness relay work ┠╴transitions_total int summed enter plus exit since startup ┖╴vanished_dirty_skips int dirty entities skipped because they left first [/codeblock] [code]transitions_total[/code] and [code]vanished_dirty_skips[/code] are cumulative, so a monitor reads them as a delta over an interval to surface churn.

method.name: interest_on_enter
method.description: Registers [param callback] for visibility entries through [param layer_id] on [param entity]. The callback receives [code](layer_id, peer_id)[/code].

method.name: interest_on_leave
method.description: Registers [param callback] for visibility exits through [param layer_id] on [param entity]. The callback receives [code](layer_id, peer_id)[/code].

method.name: interest_on_leave_policy
method.description: Sets the [enum LeavePolicy] for [param entity] on [param layer_id]. [constant LEAVE_POLICY_CUSTOM] requires [param custom_callback], called with [code](peer_id, layer_id)[/code] on server authority. Other policies reject a callback.

method.name: interest_on_perception_policy
method.description: Sets the local [enum PerceptionPolicy] for [param entity] on [param layer_id]. [constant PERCEPTION_POLICY_CUSTOM] requires [param custom_callback], which receives [code](visible, peer_id, layer_id)[/code]. A live entity reapplies perception immediately.

method.name: interest_participant_sees
method.description: Whether [param peer_id] can see [param entity] as an ordinary participant, holding a listen-server host to the same rule as any client. On the server this reads [param peer_id]'s row through [method interest_get_row]. Off the server it can only return a result for the local peer, from its own [member NetwEntity.interest] declaration. Game code asking whether a player can see an entity calls here. [method interest_wire_admits] is the one to call when the server must not be blinded to its own entities.

method.name: interest_resolved_layer_ids
method.description: The [StringName] ids of every layer [param entity] currently belongs to, sorted for stable iteration. On the server this reads the committed membership. Off the server, when the entity carries no membership yet, it returns the labels declared on the local [member NetwEntity.interest].

method.name: interest_shared_entities
method.description: Every other live [NetwEntity] that shares a layer with [param entity], excluding [param entity] itself and ordered by [member NetwEntity.entity_id]. An empty [param layer_id] searches every layer [method interest_resolved_layer_ids] returns for [param entity]. A named layer that [param entity] does not itself belong to returns no entities. On the server this reads the committed membership. Off the server, when that is empty, it scans this peer's own live entities and keeps the ones whose declared labels overlap.

method.name: interest_wire_admits
method.description: Whether traffic for [param entity] may reach [param peer_id], short-circuiting [code]true[/code] for [constant MultiplayerPeer.TARGET_PEER_SERVER] because server authority always knows every entity it holds. Every other peer falls through to [method interest_participant_sees]. Replication and spawn gating call this rather than [method interest_participant_sees], because a wire gate that hid the server's own entities from itself would stall authority rather than protect it.

method.name: lagcomp_deny_action
method.description: Rejects the action [param key] names and puts the requester back where it was. A remote requester is told over the wire, so the peer that speculated on the action reverts its own effect. A local one, and one whose peer has already left, is settled here by discarding the effect [param key] armed. Either way the rejection is the same event, which is why callers never branch on where the requester sits.

method.name: lagcomp_effect_adopt
method.description: Confirms the armed act [param key], dropping its revert and returning every [method lagcomp_effect_watch] on it. An act that is not armed is nothing to confirm.

method.name: lagcomp_effect_arm
method.description: Arms the optimistic act [param key], parking [param revert] against a deadline. The deadline is the session's own tick plus [param timeout_ticks], so an act armed during a pump expires a whole wait later rather than at whatever tick a caller happened to read first. Zero takes the session default.

method.name: lagcomp_effect_discard
method.description: Denies the armed act [param key], running the revert [method lagcomp_effect_arm] parked and returning every [method lagcomp_effect_watch] on it. An act that is not armed is nothing to deny.

method.name: lagcomp_effect_key
method.description: The key naming one predicted act, which is the one [param entity] armed at [param tick] in [param slot]. The three together are the identity, which is what lets a peer that armed an act locally recognise the server's verdict for that same act rather than for a neighbouring one. [param slot] separates two actions armed by different authorities at a single view tick, and [method Netw.action] is what assigns it.

method.name: lagcomp_effect_pending
method.description: Whether the act [param key] is armed and has neither been adopted nor discarded nor expired.

method.name: lagcomp_effect_watch
method.description: Watches the armed act [param key], returning [code]false[/code] when it is not armed. A watcher can therefore never outlive the act it observes.

method.name: lagcomp_is_configured
method.description: Whether a [NetwLagCompensationConfig] has installed on this session. Until it has, [method Netw.action] hands every authority slot zero and the rewind machinery moves nothing, so this is the absence story for the whole family rather than a null check on any one of its returns.

method.name: lagcomp_metrics
method.description: The session's lag-compensation census. The cumulative counters sum since spawn and the occupancy keys report what the session holds right now, so a reader that wants a rate takes two censuses and differences them. [codeblock lang=text] Dictionary ┠╴entities int engine records stepped this tick ┠╴timelines int rewindable entities recorded this tick ┠╴corrections int summed reconciliation snaps since spawn ┠╴max_replay_depth int worst replay window walked ┠╴consumed int summed inputs the server consumed ┠╴missing int summed input ticks stepped over as lost ┠╴folded int physics-frame callbacks folded into an existing command record ┠╴joint Dictionary joint_passes, joint_members, cells_relayed, cells_substituted, heal_snaps and linger_held, summed ┠╴pending_actions int actions queued awaiting readiness ┠╴effects_armed int optimistic effects awaiting confirm or deny ┖╴gate_fallbacks int state-ready actions resolved best-effort [/codeblock] The summed facts in [code]joint[/code] are documented on [NetwPredictStats].

method.name: lagcomp_rewind
method.description: Rewinds every entity in [param entities] to what its lag-compensation timeline held at [param tick], runs [param body] with the world in that rewound state, then restores each entity to the pose it held before the call. An entity with no timeline slot, no bound owner, or nothing recorded at [param tick] is skipped rather than rewound, and an invalid [param body] still performs the rewind and restore with nothing run in between. The rewind and the restore always pair within one call, so a caller never observes the world left in a rewound state.

method.name: lagcomp_sample
method.description: What [param entity]'s timeline held at [param tick], as a detached record. Mutating it never writes back to the timeline, and a later write to the timeline is invisible to it. [codeblock] var past := api.lagcomp_sample(entity, tick) if past.has_value(&"position"): print(past.position) [/codeblock] A query with nothing to return returns an empty record rather than [code]null[/code], so a caller reads [method NetwRecord.has_value] instead of testing for a missing object. The [RID] resolves to its wrapper here, so both overloads use the same implementation.

method.name: lagcomp_timeline_declare
method.description: Opens the lag-compensation history for [param entity], so [method lagcomp_timeline_of] starts recording its whole-entity state and input snapshots and [method lagcomp_rewind] and [method lagcomp_sample] have a past to read. Returns [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST] for a handle with no bound node. The server opens one for every entity carrying a [constant RECORD_KIND_STATE] property set, so a game declares this itself only for an entity it wants rewindable without replicated state. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the timeline was opened ┖╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST entity resolves to no bound node [/codeblock]

method.name: lagcomp_timeline_of
method.description: The [NetwTimeline] recording [param entity]'s tick-keyed state and input snapshots for lag compensation, or [code]null[/code] for a handle with no bound node or with no history declared through [method lagcomp_timeline_declare]. Not the same object as [member NetwEntity.timeline]. This one is what the server rewinds through, and returns what authority held at a past tick. That one is what prediction replays through, and returns what this peer simulated.

method.name: lagcomp_timeline_undeclare
method.description: Closes the lag-compensation history [method lagcomp_timeline_declare] opened for [param entity]. A no-op for a handle with no bound node.

method.name: liveness_allocate_route
method.description: Returns the route bound to [param wrapper]. Reserves and binds a route when needed. Repeated calls for one entity return the same route.

method.name: liveness_bind_route
method.description: Gives [param route] to [param wrapper] and announces it live, reading the wrapper's own record and owner rather than being handed them. The teardown signals are connected before [signal entity_live] is emitted, so a listener never learns a route is live while the signals that will retire it are still unconnected.

method.name: liveness_claim_routes
method.description: Creates [param count] fresh live routes and returns them, which is how a caller that owns its own records gets identity without a node or a wrapper for each one. The routes come back live, so a table row addressed to one of them is deliverable immediately. [method liveness_release_routes] is the death edge, and a route this hands out is never reissued after that. Only server authority creates routes. A client returns an empty array because routes must have one authority. [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: liveness_get_entities
method.description: Every [NetwEntity] this peer holds an [constant ENTITY_STATE_LIVE] route for, ordered by route so two calls in one frame agree. This is what this peer can see and nothing more, because a route is here only if this peer was sent the spawn.

method.name: liveness_get_routes
method.description: Every route this session currently holds live, in no promised order. A route enters the list when it binds and leaves it when it is tombstoned, so this is the whole population a delta can address. It is the read half of [method liveness_claim_routes] and [method liveness_release_routes], and a caller keeping its own index reconciles against it rather than counting the calls it made.

method.name: liveness_node_of
method.description: The root [Node] [param route] names, or [code]null[/code] once the tree has freed it.

method.name: liveness_pending_live_count
method.description: How many parked callbacks are still waiting for a binding, the liveness backlog a monitor surfaces.

method.name: liveness_poll_now
method.description: Ages every waiter registered through [method liveness_when_live] against this session's own tick, expiring the ones whose deadline has passed. A session with no configured clock polls at tick [code]0[/code], so its waiters still age by the call rather than not at all. The tick is read here rather than by the caller, which is what keeps everything driving this session agreeing on the frame a timeout is measured against.

method.name: liveness_release_routes
method.description: Retires [param routes] for the rest of the session, so a row for one of them can never be resurrected by an upsert that arrived late. A release is three acts and a caller sees none of them apart. The route is retired, its rows are dropped out of every table, and the removal is queued so the next frame tells every peer the row died. Retiring without telling anyone would leave the host alone in knowing, which is the one way a released route can outlive its release. Only server authority may release. A client returns [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNCONFIGURED] and queues nothing, while a session with no role at all releases its own routes. An empty [param routes] succeeds, because a teardown with nothing to give back is ordinary. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the routes were released, or there were none to release ┖╴ERR_UNCONFIGURED called off server authority [/codeblock]

method.name: liveness_reserve_route
method.description: Advances the route counter and returns what it handed out, binding nothing to it. Allocation is monotonic and a route is never reused, tombstone included, so a name this returns can only ever mean the entity that claims it.

method.name: liveness_route_of
method.description: The route bound to [param wrapper], or [code]0[/code].

method.name: liveness_route_state
method.description: The [enum EntityState] of [param route].

method.name: liveness_when_live
method.description: Parks [param callback] until [param route] is bound, then calls it. A watch on a route that never binds is given up on rather than kept for the session's whole life, and [param on_timeout] is how the caller learns which of the two happened. A [param timeout_ticks] of zero waits the usual amount rather than expiring immediately, because a caller that named no deadline had no opinion about one. The usual amount is one second's worth of ticks, which is the configured tickrate when a clock is running and thirty otherwise. The deadline is counted in whichever time the session actually has, so a session with no clock counts its own polls and a clocked one counts ticks. The two are never mixed.

method.name: make
method.description: Creates the stock session, or the one [param implementation] names, wrapping [param inner] when one is given and creating its own transport when none is. An [param implementation] that does not extend [NetwMultiplayer] is rejected, so a script named through [member MultiplayerTree.api_script] always inherits the stages it is replacing. Naming none keeps the stock path and pays no script dispatch for the overridable stages.

method.name: of
method.description: The session installed on [param node]'s branch, or [code]null[/code] when [param node] is outside the tree or on a branch no session returns for. It returns quietly either way, so a detached node becomes unreachable rather than raising.

method.name: participant_seat
method.description: The scene identity [param peer]'s participant is seated in, or an invalid [RID] when it holds no seat.

method.name: peer_ack
method.description: The freshest sequence [param peer] has confirmed holding, or [code]-1[/code] when it has confirmed nothing. Negative rather than zero, because zero is a sequence a peer can genuinely have acked. A per-peer delta is sent against what that peer has confirmed, which is what this records. A peer that has confirmed nothing is sent a full state rather than a delta against a baseline it never held.

method.name: peer_forget
method.description: Drops everything this session holds for [param peer]. That is its buckets, its identity, the [ResolvedJoin] it was admitted on, and its participant row, clearing [member local_participant] when [param peer] is this peer's own. The transport connection is left alone, so this is bookkeeping for a peer already gone rather than a way to remove one. [method disconnect_peer] is what closes a connection.

method.name: peer_get_accepted_join
method.description: The [ResolvedJoin] this session admitted [param peer] on, or [code]null[/code] before its join lands. This is what separates a connected peer from a joined one. [method peer_get_participant] returns [code]null[/code] for exactly the peers this returns [code]null[/code] for, so a peer that has connected and not joined is watching rather than playing.

method.name: peer_get_bucket
