method.description:
[param peer]'s instance of [param bucket_type], created on first ask. The bucket is a game authoring facility keyed by the game's own [Script] type, so two components can hold per-peer state without importing each other. [codeblock] class Bucket extends RefCounted: var ready := false
var bucket := api.peer_get_bucket(peer, Bucket) as Bucket [/codeblock] [param bucket_type] must be a script object whose [code]new()[/code] returns a [RefCounted]. Reading creates the bucket if the peer has none, so a peer the session does not hold returns [code]null[/code] and reports rather than being invented to hang a bucket on. [method peer_has_bucket] is the call when the question is whether the bucket is there. The session decides nothing here. A peer's checked credentials live on the session itself, at [method peer_get_identity]. A bucket lives exactly as long as the session holds the peer, so [method peer_forget] drops it. Instances are [RefCounted], so a handler still holding one finishes its work before it goes.

method.name: peer_get_identity
method.description: The validated [NetwIdentity] this session holds for [param peer], or [code]null[/code] when authentication never completed for it. Backs [member NetwParticipant.identity]. The session keeps these itself rather than reading them out of a [method peer_get_bucket] bucket, so there is exactly one result to who authenticated. A bucket belongs to the game and is keyed by a [Script] type, so an identity a game writes into one of its own describes the game's state and not the session's.

method.name: peer_get_participant
method.description: [param peer]'s [NetwParticipant], created on first ask and the same instance from then on, or [code]null[/code] when [method peer_get_accepted_join] returns [code]null[/code] for it. Creating is gated on the accepted join rather than on the connection, so reading this never invents a participant for a peer the session has not admitted. [method peer_forget] is what drops one.

method.name: peer_has_bucket
method.description: Whether [param peer] already holds an instance of [param bucket_type], without creating one. Ask this before [method peer_get_bucket] whenever the question is about the peer rather than about the bucket.

method.name: peer_join_address
method.description: The address another player would use to reach this session, as the live transport spells it. That is a host and port for [ENetMultiplayerPeer], and a lobby or room id for a peer whose service owns the rendezvous. Empty when nothing is live or the class has no such address.

method.name: peer_kick
method.description: Removes [param peer_id] from the session on server authority, announcing [signal peer_kicked] to that peer first when [param reason] is non-empty. A session without server authority rejects the call and removes nobody. The notice is sent before the connection closes, because a closed connection carries nothing and the kicked client would never learn why.

method.name: peer_link_stats
method.description: What the link to [param peer] is actually doing, measured rather than configured. [LocalLinkConditions] is how a test imposes a link and this is how anything reads one. The two need not agree, because a configured 8 percent loss and a measured one differ by whatever the run actually dropped. [codeblock lang=text] Dictionary ┠╴loss float lost share of the last 32 acked datagrams ┠╴rtt float seconds, the clock's averaged round trip ┠╴jitter float seconds, the clock's own deviation ┠╴reorders int datagrams that arrived behind a fresher one ┠╴duplicates int datagrams that arrived twice ┠╴mode String "good" or "bad", the send governor's own reading ┖╴budget_bits int what one datagram to this peer may spend [/codeblock] [code]mode[/code] turns [code]bad[/code] when loss or round trip crosses the governor's thresholds, and [code]budget_bits[/code] halves with it, so a link that is failing degrades instead of collapsing. It returns to [code]good[/code] only after a clean interval, and that interval doubles each time the link relapses, so a flapping link is not chased. This is a tooling-cadence read. Read it beside [method sync_explain], which returns what one row did rather than what the link did.

method.name: peer_request_kick
method.description: Asks server authority to remove [param peer_id], carrying [param reason] with the request. The server announces it as [signal peer_kick_requested] and decides. Nothing here removes anyone, which is what separates this from [method peer_kick]. The request rides a session control channel rather than a node [code]@rpc[/code], so a session with no scene tree still asks. A session that already holds authority publishes the request to itself, so the server's own handler is the single place the decision is taken.

method.name: peer_set_identity
method.description: Records [param identity] as what [method peer_get_identity] returns for [param peer]. Passing [code]null[/code] erases the row, and so does [method peer_forget] or the session's own roster teardown, because an identity outliving the peer it names would let the next peer at that id read the previous one's. Written by whatever verified the credentials, which is the auth flow on the server. A peer that never authenticated has no row rather than an empty one.

method.name: persist_set_drain
method.description: Replaces the drain a session runs at shutdown, called with no arguments and owning the whole flush of every enrolled persistence engine. With none installed the session drains on its own timer, which is the default behavior when nothing else knows when the write is finished. Install one when the game owns the shutdown story, for example to await a backend the session cannot see, and note that the installed [Callable] replaces the stock drain rather than running beside it.

method.name: persist_set_quit_guard
method.description: Replaces the guard a session arms so a quit cannot close the window before persistence has drained, called with no arguments. With none installed a host arms the tree's own quit handling. Install one when the game already owns that story, or when the session runs somewhere no [SceneTree] quit request arrives. Like [method persist_set_drain] it replaces the stock path rather than adding to it, so an installed guard is responsible for holding the quit itself.

method.name: persist_shutdown
method.description: Writes out every entity the session is saving, and does nothing on a session that saves nothing or is already shutting down. A [Callable] installed through [method persist_set_drain] replaces this and is called with no arguments. With none installed the session writes out on its own timer. Calling this more than once is safe, because the second call finds shutdown already underway and does nothing.

method.name: persist_table_commit
method.description: Claims fresh routes for the rows [param data] was saved under, writes every column of [param schema] back beneath them, and returns the route-to-save-key pairing a caller rebuilds its indexes from. An empty [param data] claims nothing and returns both empty, which is what the first play looks like. Routes are claimed fresh rather than restored, because a saved route names a row in the session that saved it and nothing in the one loading it. A column that [param data] does not carry, carries at the wrong type, or carries at the wrong length is written as zeroed storage of the declared type instead, so a save written by an older schema loads as a row with defaults rather than rejecting the whole table. A [constant COLUMN_ENTITY] column is always zeroed, because a stored entity reference names a route this load has just replaced. The whole write is fixed by one [method table_commit], so readers never observe a half-written load. [codeblock lang=text] Dictionary (param data) ┠╴ids PackedStringArray the save key for each row, in order ┖╴... Array one entry per schema column, keyed by that column's name [/codeblock] [codeblock lang=text] Dictionary (the result) ┠╴routes PackedInt64Array the route claimed for each row, same order as ids ┖╴ids PackedStringArray the save keys just claimed [/codeblock]

method.name: persist_tick_default
method.description: The persistence pass [method _persist_tick] runs when nothing overrides it, reachable so an override can defer to it. It advances every registered engine's snapshot loop by [param delta] seconds on a session that serves persistence, and does nothing on one that does not. A GDScript subclass cannot [code]super[/code] into a [code]GDVIRTUAL[/code], so this is an override's only route back to stock behaviour. An override that wants to observe the cadence rather than replace it calls this and returns.

method.name: predict_admit_frame_default
method.description: The stock verdict on one inbound prediction frame, which weighs [method sync_admit_frame_default]'s route judgement against the direction the frame travels. A route naming no entity contributes a controller of [code]0[/code], which no peer holds, so a command frame for a route this peer cannot place is rejected rather than credited to whoever sent it. Whether this peer returns as server decides which channels are admissible in which direction, so the same frame is admitted inbound on one side of a session and rejected on the other. [param payload] is judged only for emptiness here, because the decode that would read it runs after this returns [constant @GlobalScope.OK]. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the frame is admitted ┠╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST route names no known entity ┠╴ERR_SKIP the entity is lingering or dead ┠╴ERR_UNAVAILABLE the entity carries no live node ┠╴ERR_INVALID_DATA payload is empty ┖╴ERR_UNAUTHORIZED the direction this channel carries rejects this sender [/codeblock]

method.name: predict_consume
method.description: Whether authority replays a queued transition, waits, or has no transition. Uses [method _predict_consume] when overridden; otherwise uses [method predict_consume_default]. Authority replays whenever it holds a transition past [param buffer], which is zero by default, so the default result is simply whether the queue has anything in it. Raising [param buffer] moves that line and nothing else. The queue sits that much deeper and every arrival waits that much longer. Declining a transition is not free. A frame that holds still solves, so the world advances by a step belonging to no transition and the next drive spans two, which is the quantum fault [member NetwPredictStats.quantum_faults] counts.

method.name: predict_consume_default
method.description: The consume verdict [method predict_consume] returns when nothing overrides [method _predict_consume], reachable so an override can defer to it. A GDScript subclass cannot [code]super[/code] into a [code]GDVIRTUAL[/code], so this is an override's only route back to stock behaviour. An override that handles some depths and wants the default result for the rest returns this rather than reimplementing it.

method.name: predict_declare
method.description: Declares [param entity] for prediction on this peer, which is what puts it into the simulation this peer replays. An entity already declared keeps what it has. An entity whose scene declares a prediction block on its [MultiplayerSynchronizer] reaches this on tree entry, once that block has been pushed into [member NetwEntity.prediction], and a code-first caller configures that handle and calls this directly. The engine resolves its role from authority, follows [signal NetwEntity.control_changed], is rebound by the session when a move settles, and steps in the simulation loop. Only the roles this peer simulates enter that loop, so a remote display costs nothing per tick. The engine is seated against the published session rather than against this object, so a game's replaced stage is the one the engine consults. Declaring arms the rewind engine the prediction reconciles against, so a game that predicts an entity never installs a [NetwLagCompensationConfig] to turn that engine on. Arming connects the session's watch on nodes entering the tree and adopts what is already mounted, so a scene standing before the first declaration is not skipped by a watch that arrives after it. Returns [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST] when no entity stands for [param entity] here. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the entity was declared, now or already ┠╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST no entity stands for entity here ┖╴ERR_UNAVAILABLE a NetwLagCompensationConfig is declared but not yet resolved [/codeblock]

method.name: predict_drive_default
method.description: The fold the session drives with when nothing overrides [method _predict_drive]. It is published so an override can defer to it. An override reaches this the same way it reaches [method predict_consume_default]. It calls the method directly, because [code]super[/code] does not reach an override point, and returns the result for the cases it does not mean to change.

method.name: predict_engine_seated
method.description: Whether this peer runs prediction for [param entity], which is what [method predict_declare] seats and [method predict_undeclare] clears. Returning [code]false[/code] is ordinary for a body driven by another peer. It says the entity is drawn here rather than simulated here.

method.name: predict_evaluate_default
method.description: The judgement the session reaches when nothing overrides [method _predict_evaluate]. It is published so an override can defer to it. A GDScript subclass cannot [code]super[/code] into a [code]GDVIRTUAL[/code], so this is an override's only route back to stock behaviour. An override that judges one domain itself and wants the default result for the rest returns this rather than reimplementing it.

method.name: predict_flush_tap
method.description: Flushes the prediction tap's buffered lines to disk, so a capture collected while the session still runs reads complete files. A no-op while no tap is armed. The tap flushes once per second on its own and closes with the session, so most readers never need this.

method.name: predict_get_param
method.description: Reads back the prediction knob named by [param param] from [param entity]'s [NetwPredictionHandle], the same [enum PredictParam] vocabulary [method predict_set_param] writes, from [constant PREDICT_PARAM_ARCHETYPE] through [constant PREDICT_PARAM_REPLAY_BUFFER_DEPTH]. Returns [code]null[/code] when [param entity] carries no prediction handle or when [param param] names nothing this enum defines.

method.name: predict_get_stepper
method.description: The re-stepping driver [method predict_stepper_install] installed for a physics space, or [code]null[/code] when the space has none. A prediction member declaring [constant NetwPredict.SCHEDULE_STEPPED] needs its space's driver to admit replay, because replaying a stepped body means re-running the solve rather than sampling it. Without one the member runs as [constant NetwPredict.SCHEDULE_FRAME], so this returning [code]null[/code] is a downgrade rather than a failure.

method.name: predict_get_tap_cost
method.description: The prediction tap's self-reported cost, or an empty [Dictionary] while no tap is armed. What recording cost, so a capture can be read beside its own price. [codeblock lang=text] Dictionary ┠╴bytes int bytes written ┠╴lines int lines written ┠╴drains int how many times the tap was drained ┖╴mean_drain_usec float the mean wall-clock cost of one drain [/codeblock]

method.name: predict_island_add
method.description: Adds [param other] to [param entity]'s prediction island, the set of entities resimulated together because they interact. Returns [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST] when [param entity] carries no prediction handle or [param other] is not a registered entity, otherwise adds the member and returns [constant @GlobalScope.OK]. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the member was added ┖╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST entity carries no prediction handle, or other is not a registered entity [/codeblock]

method.name: predict_island_set_member_param
method.description: Writes [param value] to the per-member setting named by [param param] for [param member] inside [param entity]'s prediction island, addressed as [code](entity, member, param)[/code]. Returns [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST] when [param entity] carries no prediction handle or [param member] is not a registered entity, and [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER] when [param member] has not been added to the island with [method predict_island_add] or [param param] names nothing this enum defines. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the setting was written ┠╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST entity carries no prediction handle, or member is not a registered entity ┖╴ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER member is not in the island, or param names nothing this enum defines [/codeblock]

method.name: predict_island_set_param
method.description: Writes [param value] to the island-wide setting named by [param param] on [param entity]'s prediction island, covering [constant ISLAND_PARAM_APPROXIMATE] through [constant ISLAND_PARAM_INPUT_DELAY]. Returns [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST] when [param entity] carries no prediction handle, and [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER] when [param param] names nothing this enum defines. A count or a ticks value below zero is clamped to zero rather than rejected. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the setting was written ┠╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST entity carries no prediction handle ┖╴ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER param names nothing this enum defines [/codeblock]

method.name: predict_recover_default
method.description: The recovery plan the session makes when nothing overrides [method _predict_recover]. It is published so an override can defer to it. A GDScript subclass cannot [code]super[/code] into a [code]GDVIRTUAL[/code], so this is an override's only route back to stock behaviour. An override that plans one policy itself and wants the default result for the rest returns this rather than reimplementing it.

method.name: predict_set_corridor_callback
method.description: Installs [param callback] as [member NetwPredictionHandle.transport_corridor] on [param entity]'s prediction handle, a no-op when [param entity] has none. Only a declared corridor arms the conditional transport operator, because composing a present-time offset across a path nobody swept is how a body arrives inside a wall. Called as [code]corridor(current, proposed)[/code], and only once everything the engine can decide for itself has already passed, so it is the game's last word rather than its first. An invalid or unset [Callable] keeps the operator disabled.

method.name: predict_set_param
method.description: Writes [param value] to the prediction knob named by [param param] on [param entity]'s [NetwPredictionHandle], covering every [enum PredictParam] constant from [constant PREDICT_PARAM_ARCHETYPE] through [constant PREDICT_PARAM_REPLAY_BUFFER_DEPTH]. Does nothing when [param entity] carries no prediction handle, and logs an error rather than writing anything when [param param] names no known setting.

method.name: predict_set_sensor_callback
method.description: Declares or withdraws [param callback] as the sampler for the world fact named [param name] on [param entity]'s [member NetwPredictionHandle.sensors], a no-op when [param entity] carries no prediction handle. A valid [param callback] is stored under [param name] and an invalid one removes whatever was declared there. The declared sampler is called once before each drive and folded into the environment digest, and [method NetwPredictionHandle.sensor] is how the drive reads the sample back, so a divergence traced to the environment can be charged to it instead of left unattributed.

method.name: predict_set_simulate_callback
method.description: Replaces [param entity]'s [member NetwPredictionHandle.simulate], the single step a drive runs each tick, a no-op when [param entity] carries no prediction handle. With none installed the step defaults to the entity's owner calling [code]_network_tick(delta, tick, is_fresh)[/code] directly, and installing [param callback] routes the step through it instead, which is how a delegating node takes over the authoritative step.

method.name: predict_set_witness_callback
method.description: Installs [param callback] as [member NetwPredictionHandle.witness_contacts] on [param entity]'s prediction handle, a no-op when [param entity] has none. Called once per solved transition and expected to return the colliders the body actually touched, which is what lets a divergence be charged to a contact rather than left unattributed. An invalid or unset [Callable] is valid and leaves the witness boundary unknown, which is the absence of an observation rather than an observation of nothing.

method.name: predict_stepper_install
method.description: Installs [param stepper] as the driver [method predict_get_stepper] returns for [param space], which is what a rollback needs in order to advance the same physics space more than once inside one frame. [param stepper] is asked [method NetwPhysicsStepper._can_step] at install time, and a [code]null[/code] stepper or one returning [code]false[/code] is rejected, leaving [param space] with no driver rather than an unusable one. A member whose space has no driver still predicts, but only at [constant NetwPredict.SCHEDULE_FRAME] rather than [constant NetwPredict.SCHEDULE_STEPPED], because replaying a stepped body means re-running the solve rather than sampling it.

method.name: predict_undeclare
method.description: Removes [param entity] from prediction on this peer, dropping its engine and taking it out of the simulation loop. An identity that stands for no entity here undeclares nothing.

method.name: property_path
method.description: [param property] on [param source], relative to [param base]. Empty when either node is gone, because falling through would return a bare property name that writes whichever node the reader happened to hold. A node addresses itself as [code]"."[/code], so a property on the base is a valid self-address.

method.name: property_set_add_column
method.description: Adds [param column] as the next member of [param set], in wire order, and returns its position. The column is named on the [NetwSchema] [method property_set_create] bound the set to, so a set never mixes schemas. Returns [code]-1[/code] when [param set] names no open property set, is already sealed, names no such column on its schema, or already carries that column.

method.name: property_set_create
method.description: Opens a new [NetwPropertySet] bound to [param schema] under one [enum RecordKind], with no columns yet. Returns a null [RID] for a [param record] outside [constant RECORD_KIND_STATE], [constant RECORD_KIND_INPUT] and [constant RECORD_KIND_BROADCAST], for a [param schema] handle [NetwSchema] never declared, or for a schema carrying a strided column, which a property set cannot encode. The set stays open for [method property_set_add_column] until [method property_set_seal] closes it.

method.name: property_set_get_wire_hash
method.description: A hash over [param set]'s sealed column order and shapes, which two peers compare to confirm they agree on layout before trusting a positional decode. Returns [code]0[/code] for a [param set] handle [method property_set_create] never created.

method.name: property_set_record
method.description: The record one property set handle names, or [code]null[/code] when the handle names none. [method property_set_create] creates the handle. Modify it through [method property_set_add_column] and [method property_set_seal]. Sealed sets reject changes.

method.name: property_set_seal
method.description: Closes [param set] against further column changes, fixing its wire order and hash. Returns [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST] for a [param set] handle [method property_set_create] never created. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the set was sealed ┖╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST set names a handle property_set_create never created [/codeblock]

method.name: rpc_call
method.description: Calls [param callable] with [param args] on [param peer], where zero is every peer that may currently see the target and any other value is that one peer. [param callable]'s object must be a node an entity governs, because a remote call is addressed by [member NetwEntity.route] and a node no entity holds has none. A node with no entity at all and a node whose route is not live are counted apart and both drop the call. Neither is an error, because a call issued in the frame an entity is despawning is ordinary rather than a defect. A method the target's script neither annotates nor registers is rejected with a warning and nothing is sent, so a typo does not become a silent no-op on every peer. A local dispatch happens before anything is sent, when the method is [code]call_local[/code] and [param peer] is zero or this peer. [member relay_sender] reads this peer for the length of that call and is restored afterwards. A [code]call_remote[/code] method addressed at this peer alone is an error rather than a send. An entity passed in [param args] is encoded as its route rather than as an object, which is what lets the receiving peer resolve it to its own node.

method.name: rpc_channel_register
method.description: Registers [param handler] as the entity-lane handler for [param channel], one of the game's own reserved channels, numbered 100 to 254. A [param channel] outside that range and an invalid [param handler] are both rejected silently. Every frame that arrives on [param channel] calls [param handler] as [code](entity, payload, sender)[/code], where [code]entity[/code] is the [RID] the frame routed to, or an invalid one when the frame carried no wrapper. When [param defer_when_unknown] is true, a frame for a route not yet live waits for it rather than being dropped.

method.name: rpc_get_recipients
method.description: The peers a send for [param entity] can reach right now, which is every peer this session can see except itself. A server returns its clients, and a client returns the server together with whatever other peers its transport lets it see, so a broadcast a client authors reaches the other clients directly rather than only the server. An offline session self-dispatches through the loopback and returns the single local recipient [code]1[/code]. This returns who a message would go to rather than who can see the entity. [method interest_participant_sees] is the visibility question.

method.name: rpc_request_call
method.description: Calls [param callable] on [param peer] as a two-way request and returns the [NetwPromise] its reply settles. The request is recorded before the frame leaves, so a reply can never arrive for a request the session has not heard of. It rejects everything [method rpc_call] rejects and counts each rejection the same way, and a method that is neither registered nor annotated warns. Every rejection returns [code]null[/code] rather than a promise that never settles. [param timeout_seconds] converts to ticks against the session clock when one is configured, and against a rate of thirty otherwise, so a request still outstanding past its deadline is rejected instead of hanging.

method.name: rpc_request_call_group
method.description: Broadcasts [param callable] as a two-way request to every peer that currently sees the target entity, and returns the [NetwGroupPromise] aggregating their replies. The set of peers awaited is fixed when the request goes out, so a peer that becomes live afterwards is not owed a reply, and a peer that drops has its entry rejected. When no peer sees the entity the promise resolves through [method session_defer] rather than immediately, so a caller that has not yet attached its callbacks still sees the result. It rejects what [method rpc_request_call] rejects, and returns [code]null[/code] on each.

method.name: rpc_send_reply
method.description: Returns transaction [param txn] on [param peer] with [param value]. A returned node or [NetwEntity] crosses as a route reference the same way a call argument does, so the requester resolves it to its own instance rather than to a pointer it cannot hold.

method.name: scene_activate
method.description: Brings [param destination] up if it is not already live and forces its content root to process, returning the container it settled on or [code]null[/code] when nothing could be activated. Whatever it settles on is announced on [signal scene_activated], so one activation is always one announcement. Only a file-backed [PackedScene] can be activated. It reuses the live scene of the same name when there is one, and spawns from the packed scene's own path otherwise. A [StringName] or [String] is rejected, because a label names a live scene rather than something to build, and [method Netw.scene] is how a live one is found by label. An in-memory [PackedScene] is rejected because a peer receiving the spawn has no path to load it from, and a [Node] is rejected because an already-mounted node is not something to activate. [codeblock lang=text] DESTINATION_PACKED -> the live container, else a spawn DESTINATION_PACKED_UNPATHED -> rejected DESTINATION_NAME -> rejected DESTINATION_NODE -> rejected DESTINATION_NONE -> rejected [/codeblock] [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: scene_add_player
method.description: Seats [param player] at [param scene]. The server admits the player and parents its node under the scene's content root, so the node is where a visitor would look for it. The server then watches that node so the seat survives a re-admit, and flushes interest in the same act. Rejects [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAVAILABLE] when [param player] holds no node or [param scene] holds no content root to seat it under. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the seat was granted ┠╴ERR_UNAVAILABLE player holds no node, scene holds no content root, or the admission did not take ┠╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST scene holds no live node to admit into ┖╴ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER player's peer id is 0 [/codeblock] [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: scene_admit
method.description: Admits [param peer] to [param scene], returning [constant @GlobalScope.OK] only once the admission has taken. This is the guarded admission. It rejects peer zero, rejects a scene whose node is gone, and re-reads [method scene_admits] afterwards rather than trusting the write, so a caller is told what actually happened instead of what was attempted. A successful admission calls [method interest_flush_now] in the same act, so the peer just admitted can see the scene without waiting for anything else to drive a flush. A rejected admission changes nothing. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the peer was admitted ┠╴ERR_UNAUTHORIZED called off server authority ┠╴ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER peer is 0 ┠╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST scene names no live node ┖╴ERR_UNAVAILABLE the admission did not take [/codeblock] [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: scene_admits
method.description: Whether [param scene] currently admits [param peer], read from the scene's [NetwInterestLayer] rather than from a list of its own, so an admission the layer revoked is not still reported here.

method.name: scene_change_to_file
method.description: Changes to the file-backed scene at [param path], mirroring [method SceneTree.change_scene_to_file] while keeping the change under server authority. [param scope] says who the change is for and nothing infers it, so the same call means the same thing on a listen host and on a dedicated server. [param requester] names the node the change is asked from, which resolves the participant a [constant SCENE_CHANGE_PARTICIPANT] change moves and the source world a [constant SCENE_CHANGE_SCENE] change replaces. A scope that needs one and finds none is rejected rather than widened. On authority the change applies directly. On a client it becomes a [method scene_request] whose result settles the returned [NetwPromise]. [codeblock] var promise := session.scene_change_to_file(self, "res://arena.tscn") await promise.wait() [/codeblock]

method.name: scene_change_to_packed
method.description: Changes to a file-backed [param packed] scene, mirroring [method SceneTree.change_scene_to_packed]. A scene with no resource path is rejected with [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAVAILABLE], because another peer has no path it can load. [method scene_change_to_file] says what [param scope] means.

method.name: scene_create
method.description: Spawns a scene from [param recipe] and declares it, returning the scene entity's [RID] or an invalid one when the spawn produced nothing. A [code]null[/code] [param recipe] builds an empty scene, which is somewhere to admit players and nothing more. [param isolation] declares whether this one scene hosts its own world, as a [enum SceneIsolation]. It rides the spawn, so two scenes in one session may differ. [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: scene_declare
method.description: Makes [param entity] a scene, so it can admit players and hold the nodes that belong to it. Server authority may declare anything, and any peer may declare an entity whose route it already holds, because the server admitted that route. A client repeating a scene the server declared is following rather than inventing. A peer with neither authority nor a route returns [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAUTHORIZED], because it would be inventing a scene the session never declared. Declare this before the entity is armed. A bound entity returns [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNCONFIGURED]. If the entity has no record yet, the session stores the declaration until [method entity_bind_node] creates the record. [codeblock] var mirror := api.entity_create() api.entity_bind_route(mirror, route) # the server's route api.scene_declare(mirror) # OK, this is a mirror [/codeblock] Reversed by [method scene_undeclare], which drops the label with the facet. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the facet was written, or parked for arming ┠╴ERR_UNAUTHORIZED called with neither server authority nor entity's own route ┠╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST entity is not a valid handle ┖╴ERR_UNCONFIGURED entity is already armed with a node [/codeblock]

method.name: scene_destroy
method.description: Unparents and frees [param scene]'s live node on the spot, returning whether one was found. Nothing is drained and nothing waits, so anything still in flight for that scene is dropped. A [param scene] that returns no live container returns [code]false[/code] silently, because destroying what is already gone is the caller's intended end state.

method.name: scene_find
method.description: A live scene whose stem is [param stem], or an invalid [RID]. Stems are not unique, so this returns "an instance of this stem" rather than "the one", resolving to the most recent live instance. Use [method scene_find_all] wherever the difference between an instance and every one of them can change the outcome.

method.name: scene_find_all
method.description: Every live scene whose stem is [param stem], which is every instance of one level. The [method scene_list] reading narrowed to one stem's instances.

method.name: scene_get_current
method.description: The scene this peer presents while it still resolves to a mounted container, or an invalid [RID] once it does not, which is the session's one result to the question. A dedicated server presents nothing and always returns invalid. The presentation is recomputed from what the session seats this peer in rather than written by whatever changed, so a scene arriving, leaving or re-seating this peer all settle here, and the mounted check means a caller is never handed a detached scene to pass onward.

method.name: scene_get_entities
method.description: The RIDs of the entities seated under [param scene]'s container, in no guaranteed order. A scene that returns no live container returns an empty array rather than rejecting, because asking about what is gone is an ordinary question.

method.name: scene_get_label
method.description: The name [param scene] goes by, which is its declared label when it carries one and its node's name otherwise. A scene is identified by its [RID] and never by this string, because two live copies of one arena share a name and admit players separately.

method.name: scene_get_layer
method.description: The [NetwInterestLayer] that decides who sees [param scene]. A layer the session has declared is created on the spot if it is not live yet, so a caller adding viewers to a scene's layer never needs a second call. A layer the session never declared returns an invalid [RID] rather than being invented.

method.name: scene_get_local_player
method.description: This peer's own player entity while it is seated at [param scene], or an invalid [RID] when this peer presents some other scene or presents none. The per-scene slice of [member local_player].

method.name: scene_get_node
method.description: The live container node [param scene] stands for, or [code]null[/code] when it holds no mounted node. The read a caller that mounts, frees, or reparents a scene wants, because those acts are performed against the container rather than against the identity.

method.name: scene_get_param
method.description: Reads one [enum SceneParam] knob off [param scene]. A scene the session never bound returns [code]null[/code] rather than rejecting, and a knob that holds no value returns [code]null[/code] too, because an absent knob and an unset one are the same question here.

method.name: scene_get_participants
method.description: The participants seated at [param scene], read from the scene's interest layer. The roster row behind each seated peer, rather than the peer id itself.

method.name: scene_get_players
method.description: The player entities in [param scene]. [member players] contains the players from every live scene.

method.name: scene_is_declared
method.description: Whether [param entity] declares itself a scene. An entity the session never bound returns [code]false[/code] rather than rejecting, because asking about a stranger is an ordinary question.

method.name: scene_list
method.description: Every live scene the session holds, in no guaranteed order. A scene is live while its container is mounted, so a declared-but-unentered scene returns nothing here and a despawned one drops out without a caller refreshing anything.

method.name: scene_move
method.description: Moves [param entity] under [param destination]'s container, returning the [NetwPromise] the settle carries. The mover is reparented on every peer by the same carry rules, so the promise resolves [constant @GlobalScope.OK] only once the entity stands under its new scene everywhere it exists. A carry masks the mover off the physics server before the parent swap and restores it after, spending two [signal SceneTree.physics_frame]s on each side. The physics server drops a body from an [Area2D]'s or [Area3D]'s overlap tracking only on a step, and a body still tracked re-emits [signal Area2D.body_entered] out of its own [signal Node.tree_entered] as the swap remounts it. That signal fires while the body is in the tree and its children are not, so a handler reading a child of the body sees an orphan. The window is what stops it, and a mover with no [member CollisionObject2D.collision_layer] or [member CollisionObject2D.collision_mask] skips the window because it has nothing to evict. A move asked off server authority returns [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAUTHORIZED] on a promise that has already settled. [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: scene_observe
method.description: Registers [param callback] for one scene [param event] on [param scene]. An invalid [param scene] or an unset [param callback] registers nothing, and registering the same [param callback] twice stores it once, so an edge is heard once. [param event] is a raw ordinal mirroring the [code]NetwMultiplayer.SceneEvent[/code] enum, which stays the one published spelling. Plural where a layer monitor is singular, because several unrelated observers legitimately watch one scene while a layer's monitor is the session's own. The registration names the scene [RID] rather than a node, so it survives whichever node currently stands in for that scene. A callback retires itself by returning [code]true[/code], and one returning anything else, including nothing, is kept. That is the only way to drop one registration when several share a base [Callable]. [method scene_unobserve] matches with [code]==[/code], and a bound [Callable] compares equal on its base and the number of values bound rather than on the values themselves, so two callbacks that bind different subscribers cannot be told apart. An observer whose object has been freed is dropped on the next dispatch without being called, so retiring is for a live observer that has decided it is finished.

method.name: scene_packed_stem
method.description: The name [param packed] would be declared under, which is its root node's name. Returns empty for a [PackedScene] with no state or no root node.

method.name: scene_participant_viewport
method.description: The [SubViewport] holding the world this peer's participant sees, or [code]null[/code] when it sees none. Only a listen host resolves one, because a client's world is mounted under its own window and a dedicated server renders nothing. It is resolved in this order, and the first match wins. - the scene the local player is seated in, so a host standing in a world draws the world it stands in - [method scene_get_current], so a host between players draws the scene it was admitted to rather than an arbitrary live one - the first live scene that owns its world and whose level still runs, which is what a spectator sees A scene declaring [constant SCENE_ISOLATION_OWN_WORLD] is the only kind mounted in a [SubViewport], so a scene sharing the session's world is passed over at every step. [signal participant_viewport_changed] announces a turn-over, and [HostSceneView] is the stock consumer of both.

method.name: scene_release
method.description: Removes [param peer] from [param scene], returning whether anything was done. The peer is told before the seat is taken away, while it still holds the seat that names what it is losing. A client learns its membership from the scene entity, so a peer released the other way round would keep presenting a scene it no longer belongs to. A successful release calls [method interest_flush_now], as [method scene_admit] does, so the peer stops receiving the scene in the same act. [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: scene_reload_current
method.description: Re-enters the file-backed scene this peer currently presents, mirroring [method SceneTree.reload_current_scene]. A peer presenting no scene, or one created without a resource path, receives [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAVAILABLE].

method.name: scene_request
method.description: Asks server authority to move the local player to the scene file at [param path]. A label cannot be requested, because [method Netw.scene] is what resolves a live scene by label and a change names a path. The promise rejects with [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAUTHORIZED] when policy rejects, [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_SKIP] when a newer request supersedes it, and [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_TIMEOUT] when authority never returns within ten seconds. [b]Player request.[/b]

method.name: scene_set_carry_move
method.description: Replaces the physics-guarded carry that [method scene_move] runs when it moves an entity between scenes. [param carry] receives [code](mover, destination_node, opts, promise)[/code] and owns everything from the guard to settling [code]promise[/code], which is why it is handed the promise rather than returning a value. With none installed the session carries the move itself. Install one to guard a body this session cannot know how to suppress, or to watch what a move is handed.

method.name: scene_set_host_view_factory
method.description: Replaces the node a listen-server host draws its own player's world into, as [code]func(root: Node) -> Node[/code]. The session calls it once when [member role] is [constant ROLE_LISTEN_SERVER] and the live scene owns its own world, names the result [code skip-lint]HostSceneView[/code] and parents it under the root it was handed. Returning [code]null[/code] leaves the display alone. With none installed the session makes a stock [HostSceneView], and makes nothing when a [ParticipantView] already stands under the root, so a game that placed its own view keeps it. Install one only to build a different node entirely.

method.name: scene_set_param
method.description: Writes one [enum SceneParam] knob on [param scene], returning [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST] when the session holds no record for it. These belong to the scene rather than to the session. What a scene is called and whether it carries its own world are per-scene facts and this is where they are written. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the knob was written ┠╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST scene names no record, or SCENE_PARAM_PROCESSING names no live node ┠╴ERR_UNCONFIGURED param is SCENE_PARAM_ISOLATION and the scene is already bound ┖╴ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER param names no known knob [/codeblock]

method.name: scene_undeclare
method.description: Stops [param entity] being a scene, dropping the label and isolation it declared. This is the reverse of [method scene_declare] under the same rules. Server authority may undeclare anything, a peer holding the entity's route may undeclare its own copy, and a peer with neither returns [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAUTHORIZED]. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the facet was cleared, or parked for arming ┠╴ERR_UNAUTHORIZED called with neither server authority nor entity's own route ┠╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST entity is not a valid handle ┖╴ERR_UNCONFIGURED entity is already armed with a node [/codeblock]

method.name: scene_unobserve
method.description: Reverses [method scene_observe] for one [param callback]. Removing something never registered is inert rather than an error.

method.name: schema_add_column
method.description: Appends [param key] to [param schema] in address order. A column of one value per row leaves [param stride] at its default. Duplicate keys, invalid types, invalid strides, and additions after sealing return [code]-1[/code].

method.name: schema_create
method.description: The handle for the schema named [param name], creating one when this session holds none. Declaring a name that already exists returns the handle it already has and restarts that schema's re-declaration cursor, so a script reload replays its own columns rather than creating a second schema.

method.name: schema_find
method.description: The handle this session holds for [param name], or an invalid [RID] when it holds none. This is the lookup alone and it compiles nothing, so a declaration this session has not taken in returns an invalid handle. [method schema_find_or_adopt] is the call that takes one in.

method.name: schema_find_or_adopt
method.description: The handle this session holds for [param name], compiling the declaration first when the process-wide schema registry has one this session never adopted. This is [method schema_find] with the lazy adopt attached, and it exists because a class's [code]static var[/code] initializers run on first access rather than at load, so a schema can be declared after the session already swept the registry. An unknown registry name returns an invalid result without adopting anything.

method.name: schema_get_column_count
method.description: The number of columns fixed into [param schema], or zero when the handle is unknown.

method.name: schema_get_column_key
method.description: The key at [param column], or an empty [StringName] when either address is unknown.

method.name: schema_get_column_stride
method.description: The number of elements one row occupies at [param column], or zero when either address is unknown.

method.name: schema_get_column_type
method.description: The column type fixed at [param column], or [code]-1[/code] when either address is unknown.

method.name: schema_get_element_type
method.description: The [enum Variant.Type] one element of [param type] reads as, or [code]-1[/code] when [param type] is outside the column vocabulary. [constant COLUMN_VARIANT] returns [constant @GlobalScope.TYPE_NIL] because its elements are self-describing.

method.name: schema_get_hash
method.description: The fixed shape hash for [param schema], or zero before sealing and for an unknown handle.

method.name: schema_get_name
method.description: The caller-facing name held by [param schema], or an empty [StringName] when the handle is unknown.

method.name: schema_seal
method.description: Fixes [param schema]'s declaration order and shape hash. A changed or truncated re-declaration returns [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNCONFIGURED]. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the schema is sealed ┠╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST schema names nothing valid ┠╴ERR_INVALID_DECLARATION the schema declares more columns than the row mask carries ┖╴ERR_UNCONFIGURED an open re-declaration did not match what was sealed before [/codeblock]

method.name: schema_set_column_quantizer
method.description: Assigns [param quantizer] to [param column] before [param schema] is sealed. A sealed declaration is unchanged.

method.name: send_auth
method.description: Sends [param data] to [param id] as one packet of [member inner]'s own authentication protocol, while that peer is still authenticating. Returns [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNCONFIGURED] when this session wraps no [member inner], and otherwise whatever the wrapped [SceneMultiplayer] returns. [method complete_auth] ends the handshake this data rides. Both keep [SceneMultiplayer]'s own spelling, so a game swapping one session for the other finds the authentication handshake under the same names.

method.name: send_bytes
method.description: Sends [param bytes] as a raw packet to [param id], or to every connected peer when [param id] is [code]0[/code], over [param mode] on [param channel]. Returns [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNCONFIGURED] before a [MultiplayerPeer] is installed, otherwise the underlying peer's own send result.

method.name: send_to
method.description: Sends one payload to [param peer], choosing for itself how it travels. This is the only send the session publishes, because choosing among the three ways a payload can leave needs the clock and the channel declaration both. [codeblock lang=text] peer is us dispatched locally, never framed clock set, channel groups appended to that peer's run and sent at the next tick otherwise framed and sent now [/codeblock] Grouping waits on the tick, so a session with no configured clock always sends now. A buffered payload in a session whose clock never runs would sit in the run forever. A negative [param route] is rejected with [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER], because it addresses no entity and no peer either. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the payload was dispatched, sent, or staged ┠╴ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER route is negative ┖╴ERR_UNCONFIGURED the session has no dispatcher to note a staged send with [/codeblock]

method.name: service_clear
method.description: Drops every registered service. Silent, because a session that is ending announces its own end and a per-service notice would repeat what every listener has already been told.

method.name: service_get
method.description: The service registered under [param type], or [code]null[/code]. A service the game freed reads as absent, because the session holds an id rather than a reference and would otherwise keep the object alive past the scene that made it. [param type] is a [Script] for a service written in GDScript and the class itself for one the extension registers, so [code skip-lint]service_get(LobbyDirectory)[/code] and [code skip-lint]service_get(MyGamestate)[/code] are the same call. A class reference is normalized to its name once and cached for the session, because deriving the name costs an instantiation.

method.name: service_get_all
method.description: Every service whose script is [param base] or derives from it, in registration order.

method.name: service_get_named
method.description: The service registered under the class named [param class_name], or [code]null[/code]. This is how a service written in C++ is reached. [method service_register] keys a service by its [method Object.get_class] when it carries no script, so a service with no script is found by name where one with a script is found by its [Script]. [codeblock] var directory := api.service_get_named(&"LobbyDirectory") [/codeblock]

method.name: service_register
method.description: Registers [param service] under [param type], defaulting to its own script, and emits [signal service_registered]. Re-registering the identical instance is inert, because a service that auto-registers on entering the tree may also be registered explicitly.

method.name: service_unregister
method.description: The twin of [method service_register], honoured only while [param type] still names [param service].

method.name: session_answer_probe
method.description: Returns one [code]NPRB[/code] server-browser probe from [param peer], which rides the same authentication phase a join does and is consumed here rather than reaching the join path. The reply body comes from the provider declared through [method Netw.configure_server_info] for this session, or from the built-in [method NetwServerInfo.from_session] reading of live session state when no declaration governs it. A declaration this session can no longer reach rejects the probe with [constant NetwAuthProtocol.PROBE_ERROR] rather than falling back to the built-in reply. A probe is rejected with a busy status rather than a body when more than ten arrive within one second, or when more than thirty-two peers are still tracked as probing. Both limits are per session and a rejected probe still counts against them, so a flood cannot buy itself a fresh budget by being rejected. [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: session_cancel_deferred
method.description: Withdraws [param key] from the deferral queue, for a caller that did the work on the spot and has nothing left to settle. An unqueued key is not an error.

method.name: session_defer
method.description: Schedules [param fn] to run at the next flush. Scheduling a [param key] that is already queued moves it to the back rather than queueing it twice, which is how a call asks to run after whatever scheduled it. An empty key is never merged, so unkeyed calls run in the order they were scheduled. This is not [method Object.call_deferred]. The queue drains to a fixed point rather than once, so a callback that schedules more work still runs within the same flush, and coalescing by key is what keeps a cascade of admissions and releases to one pass of effect instead of one per edge. [method session_flush_deferred] is the door that drains it and [method session_cancel_deferred] withdraws a key. A flush may run game callbacks, so a caller holding a lock or iterating its own collection defers rather than flushes.

method.name: session_flush_deferred
method.description: Drains everything [method session_defer] queued, repeatedly, until a pass adds nothing new. Every tree change a game made is settled here, so this is where a move, a death and a lost copy are decided and reported. The session calls it on its own. Call it to read a settled result before the next frame, once the tree changes are done. Do not call it from inside a [signal Node.tree_entered] or [signal Node.tree_exiting] handler, because an enclosing [method Node.reparent] is still between its removal and its addition and the tree it would return from is not the final one. An authoritative owner still detached when the queue drains has ended its life rather than moved. A queue that settles is silent. One still holding keys after the internal pass bound pushes an error naming them, because a row that reschedules itself every pass is a cycle in the caller's own scheduling rather than something the queue can resolve, and a defect that hangs is worse than one that reports. The session's own tick and an explicit call both come through here, so a cycle is reported once wherever it is reached rather than being swallowed by whichever caller drained first. It may run a game's callbacks. This is not [method embed_settle], which finishes starting the session up.

method.name: session_flush_tick
method.description: Runs everything one tick sends. It flushes interest when a layer driver is installed, sends for every registered writer at [param tick], services the transport, then settles and clears what the tick retired. That order matters. The flush stamps each datagram with its sequence, and servicing the transport first would acknowledge a sequence this tick had not written yet. The session connects this to [signal clock_after_tick] when it is built, ahead of any game listener, so a game reading [signal clock_after_tick] reads a tick whose frames have already gone out. An interest flush that rejects stops the rest of the tick and returns why. A game never calls this. It is published for a custom driver that owns its own tick source and therefore has to run the pass the clock would have run.

method.name: session_get_all
method.description: Every session that [method session_is_active] returns true for, in the order they were created. A session enters this list when it is constructed and leaves it when it is freed. The registry behind it holds ids rather than references, so it never keeps a session alive, and a read is the one place an id whose session is gone is dropped. A caller therefore reads a list of live sessions without a disposal hook existing anywhere. [codeblock] var sessions := NetwMultiplayer.session_get_all() if sessions.size() == 1: # exactly one session is installed, so it is unambiguous pass [/codeblock]

method.name: session_get_authored_role
method.description: The role the game asked for, read live off [member NetwSessionConfig.desired_role] on the config [method session_get_config] returns. [member role] is what the session actually became, and this is what was asked of it. The two agree once a connection has resolved, and they part while a game has changed the config and nothing has connected since. A config carrying a value outside [enum Role] returns [constant ROLE_LISTEN_SERVER], which is what a session with no configuration already intends.

method.name: session_get_config
method.description: The values this session consumed from the [NetwSessionConfig] a game declared with [method Netw.configure_session], or a default one until a declaration is consumed. Never [code]null[/code], so a session that declared nothing still returns [member NetwSessionConfig.app_id] and [member NetwSessionConfig.link_conditions] with defaults. Reading the config is what applies it, taking the role it asked for and arming authentication, so a session whose config was never read runs no authentication at all. The result is freshly built on every call and is not connected to the session. The session copied the declared config once and owns the copy, so writing to what this returns changes nothing and is not reported either. [method session_set_server_info] is the one value a running session takes back, because it is the only one collected after the configuration has settled. This is where a caller reads what the session was configured with, by reading a field off the result.

method.name: session_get_join_schema
method.description: The wire parameters the join handler [method Netw.configure_join] installed declares, so a Join form can be drawn without knowing the game. Empty when no handler is installed or the handler asked for no wire argument. It sits beside [method session_prepare_join] because it describes what that verb accepts, not how a session is brought up. [codeblock lang=text] Array[Dictionary] ┖╴entry ┠╴name String the argument's name, or "argN" when the handler names none ┠╴type int a Variant.Type value ┠╴class_name StringName empty, no argument here is object-typed ┖╴default Variant always null [/codeblock]

method.name: session_is_active
method.description: Whether the [SceneTree] resolves this session for its own root path, which is what makes a session the one a node on that branch reaches through [member Node.multiplayer]. One question returns both install shapes. A branch-scoped session is installed at the path its [SceneMultiplayer] roots at, a tree-wide session roots at [code]/root[/code] and is the tree's default, and [method SceneTree.get_multiplayer] resolves either by walking up from the path, so neither shape needs a test of its own.

method.name: session_leave
method.description: Flushes persistence, closes the active peer, and returns to [constant SESSION_STATE_OFFLINE]. It waits up to three seconds for the server to acknowledge the departure, so a caller that awaits the returned promise knows the peer is closed rather than closing. A session already at [constant SESSION_STATE_OFFLINE], and one with no scene tree to time the window with, both return a promise that is already settled. [codeblock] var left := api.session_leave() if not left.is_settled: await left.wait() [/codeblock]

method.name: session_notify_shutdown
method.description: Warns every live peer that this server is going away, carrying [param reason], and announces [signal session_server_disconnecting] locally as well. A session without server authority rejects the call and warns nobody. The notice rides a session control channel rather than a node [code]@rpc[/code], so a session with no scene tree still warns its clients. Nothing here closes a peer, so the server still has to tear itself down afterwards.

method.name: session_pause
method.description: Suspends the game on every live peer, each receiving [signal session_tree_paused] carrying [param reason], and on this session too. A session without server authority rejects the call and pauses nobody. The local announcement is made through the same channel decode a remote peer takes, so the host cannot end up in a pause state its clients disagree with.

method.name: session_prepare_join
method.description: Prepares [param username] and [param args] as the local player's join, without assigning a transport peer. It checks the identity, arms authentication, runs the declared [NetwAuthFlow]'s credential step, and holds what authentication will send until the peer is assigned. A client submits it on reaching [constant SESSION_STATE_ONLINE]. A server holds it until [method session_submit_join] is called. The [enum @GlobalScope.Error] travels as the promise's [member NetwPromise.result], so a caller reads [code]int(prepared.result)[/code]. A flow with no credential preparation to run returns a promise that is already settled, so it never suspends. [codeblock] var prepared := api.session_prepare_join(&"Dev") if not prepared.is_settled: await prepared.wait() if int(prepared.result) != OK: return [/codeblock] An empty [param username] returns [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER] without running the flow. [b]Player request.[/b]

method.name: session_request_leave
method.description: Asks server authority for permission to leave, carrying [param reason]. The server announces it as [signal session_disconnect_requested] and decides. Nothing here closes a peer or leaves a session. A session that already holds authority publishes the request to itself, so the server's own handler is the single place the decision is taken.

method.name: session_role_name
method.description: The display name of [param role], with the [enum Role] constants' [code]ROLE_[/code] prefix dropped, so [constant ROLE_LISTEN_SERVER] returns [code]"LISTEN_SERVER"[/code]. A role outside [enum Role] returns the empty string rather than a made-up name, because a label is only ever shown and must not invent a role that does not exist. This is the spelling every debug surface reports a role under, so a reader comparing a snapshot, a session event and the editor panel sees one vocabulary.

method.name: session_set_join_resolver
method.description: Sets the join resolver. It is called as [code]resolver(username, args, sender)[/code] and returns a [ResolvedJoin] to admit or [code]null[/code] to reject. Without a resolver, the session accepts the claimed username.

method.name: session_set_role
method.description: Declares what this peer is, so [member role], [member is_host] and [member is_local_client] all return from [param role] at once. This records what the session became, where [method session_get_authored_role] records what was asked for. It is written once the transport has said which end this peer is on, which is why a client waiting to connect can return [constant ROLE_CLIENT] before any connection exists.

method.name: session_set_root
method.description: Installs [param reader] as the [Callable] [member root] returns from. It takes no arguments and returns the node, which is what lets the result follow a re-mount without anything here being told about it. A [Callable] rather than a stored node, because the root is derived from the transport's own relative-addressing path and re-resolves when that path changes. A node pushed once would go stale silently, and a stale root parents a session's own views under a branch that is no longer in the tree.

method.name: session_set_server_info
method.description: Replaces the [NetwServerInfo] this host returns a probe from, which [method Netw.configure_session] declares before a session starts and a lobby screen only learns when a player names their server. It is copied on the way in, so the caller keeps no live handle and a later edit of what it passed changes nothing here. [code]null[/code] clears it, and a probe then returns only what the session knows by itself, which is its app id and its live player count. This is a value rather than a provider, so it says what does not change while this host runs. [method Netw.configure_server_info] is the provider a game declares when the result is computed per probe, and it wins where both exist, because a provider is handed the value set here as the record it edits. Only a host is ever asked for one, but this takes the value at any role and without a transport, because a lobby collects the name before it knows which end it will be.

method.name: session_set_state
method.description: Puts the session machine in [param state] without asking whether the edge is legal, announcing [signal session_state_changed] when the value actually moves. [method session_transition] is the guarded call and is what connecting and disconnecting use. This one is for a caller restoring a state rather than reaching it, such as a session reset to [constant SESSION_STATE_OFFLINE] after a failure left it part way. Using this where [method session_transition] would do hides an illegal move instead of reporting it.

method.name: session_submit_join
method.description: Submits [param username] and [param args] as the local player's join request. The request rides the session's own join channel rather than a node [code]@rpc[/code], so a session with no scene tree still joins. A server submits to itself locally. A join prepared by [method session_prepare_join] is consumed when it is submitted, so the automatic submit when the session comes online and an explicit call here cannot both send it. An empty [param username] submits nothing. [b]Player request.[/b]

method.name: session_transition
method.description: Moves the session machine to [param state] through the edge rules, announcing [signal session_state_changed] on the way. A move to the state it already holds does nothing, and a move the session does not allow is reported rather than performed, so an impossible transition shows up where it was asked for. This is what connecting and disconnecting use. [method session_set_state] is the unguarded write, for a caller restoring a state rather than reaching one.

method.name: session_unpause
method.description: Resumes the game on every live peer, each receiving [signal session_tree_unpaused], and on this session too. A session without server authority rejects the call and resumes nobody. The twin of [method session_pause]. It carries no reason and does not check that a pause came first, because a peer that missed the pause must still end up resumed.

method.name: spawn_admit_frame_default
method.description: The stock verdict on one inbound spawn, despawn or reparent frame, and what an override of [method _spawn_admit_frame] narrows rather than replaces. Only the server spawns, so [param sender] is judged before anything else and any other peer returns [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAUTHORIZED] whatever channel it named. A channel this does not admit, or an empty [param payload], returns [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_INVALID_DATA]. [param route] is unresolved by construction, because the frame that creates a route arrives before that route exists. It travels so an override can read it. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the frame is admitted ┠╴ERR_UNAUTHORIZED sender is not the server ┖╴ERR_INVALID_DATA channel does not carry spawn, despawn, hide or reparent traffic, or payload is empty [/codeblock]

method.name: spawn_construct_default
method.description: The stock body of [method _spawn_construct]. It builds the node from the constructor the spawn pump armed for this materialization, and returns [code]null[/code] when the pump armed none.

method.name: spawn_declare_default
method.description: The stock verdict on declaring [param entity] eligible for materialization, and what an override of [method _spawn_declare] narrows or adds to rather than replaces. [constant @GlobalScope.OK] if this peer holds a wrapper for [param entity], [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST] otherwise. [param recipe] travels unread so an override can validate or enrich it before declaring. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK this peer holds a wrapper for entity ┖╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST this peer holds no wrapper for entity [/codeblock]

method.name: spawn_register_constructor
method.description: Registers [param function] under [param id], so [method spawn_registered] can reconstruct it on a peer that has no host node to read it from. [param arg_types] and [param quantizers] declare positionally how [param function]'s arguments cross the wire. Declaring them keys the argument schema to [param id], which is how the wire already addresses the recipe, so a [param function] whose object carries no [Script] still encodes and decodes. Declaring neither reads the schema off the host script instead, which then has to return identically on every peer. A schema is never negotiated. Every peer registers [param id] itself and decodes with what it registered, so two peers declaring different schemas for one id read different values out of the same bytes.

method.name: spawn_registered
method.description: Runs the constructor registered under [param id] on every peer and returns the local entity handle. The same act for a session with no host node. The recipe is an id both sides already hold rather than a reference only the sender has.

method.name: stats_get
method.description: One counter of [method stats_snapshot], selected by [param stat]. A [param stat] outside the enum returns [code]0[/code].

method.name: stats_get_verdict_count
method.description: How many times this session has returned [param verdict] while replicating. The count runs for the life of the session and [method clear] is what resets it.

method.name: stats_snapshot
method.description: Every [enum NetwMultiplayer.Stat] value, keyed by the lowercase name of its constant. Counters and current totals come back in one snapshot, so a reader wanting a rate takes two snapshots and subtracts, rather than asking for each number separately and getting readings from different moments. Every value in [enum Stat] is present in every result and reads zero where there is nothing to report, so a reader never has to tell a zero apart from a value this build does not publish. [method stats_get] is the same snapshot read one value at a time.

method.name: sync_admit_frame_default
method.description: The default result for one arriving replication frame, admitting it only when its route is alive, its [param channel] is one that carries replication, and its [param payload] holds something. This runs before anything is decoded, so a rejected frame costs a route lookup and nothing more. A route the session cannot place is [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST], a route on its way out is [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_SKIP], a route whose entity no longer stands is [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAVAILABLE], and a wrong channel or an empty payload is [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_INVALID_DATA]. The channels admitted are [constant NetwFrameEnvelope.SYNC], [constant NetwFrameEnvelope.SYNC_ROW], [constant NetwFrameEnvelope.SYNC_ROW_DELTA], [constant NetwFrameEnvelope.SYNC_ROW_WINDOW] and [constant NetwFrameEnvelope.SYNC_DELTA]. [param sender], [param comp], [param flags] and [param tick] travel so a game overriding the gate can judge the whole header, and the stock verdict reads none of them. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the frame is admitted ┠╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST route names no known entity ┠╴ERR_SKIP the entity is lingering or dead ┠╴ERR_UNAVAILABLE the entity carries no live node ┖╴ERR_INVALID_DATA channel does not carry replication, or payload is empty [/codeblock]

method.name: sync_apply_set_default
method.description: The stock body of [method _sync_apply_set]. It writes [param values] through the applier installed for the running stage, or returns [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNCONFIGURED] outside one.

method.name: sync_explain
method.description: Why one row did or did not reach one peer on the last send, read from what the session already holds rather than from a log. This is for a debug overlay rather than for a tick. It walks no history and records nothing, but it is not cheap enough to call every frame. A route the session has never offered to [param peer] returns a [code]verdict[/code] of [code]unoffered[/code] and leaves the rest empty. [codeblock lang=text] Dictionary ┠╴verdict String "sent", "deferred", "caught_up", "ungathered", "rejected" or "unoffered" ┠╴tick int the datagram base tick the verdict was taken at ┠╴sticky int the columns owed to this peer and not yet confirmed ┠╴in_flight int staged rows this peer has neither acked nor lost ┖╴has_baseline bool whether a delta may be sent at all [/codeblock] [code]deferred[/code] means the tick ran out of budget for the row, which keeps the priority it has built up so a later pass outranks whatever kept beating it. [code]caught_up[/code] means the peer already holds every column. [code]rejected[/code] means the frame could not be written or the encode turned it down. [code]ungathered[/code] means the values never became a row at all. Read this beside [method peer_link_stats], which returns what the link did rather than what one row did.

method.name: sync_gather_set_default
method.description: The stock body of [method _sync_gather_set]. It reads the gatherer installed for the running stage, or returns an empty array outside one.

method.name: sync_note_ack_default
method.description: Advances the sync pipeline's baseline for [param peer] to [param sequence], and what an override of [method _sync_note_ack] adds to rather than replaces. The receiving twin of [method sync_note_sent_default]. A peer whose acknowledgements stop moving keeps its old baseline, so its deltas grow rather than going wrong. A session that replicates nothing records nothing.

method.name: sync_note_sent_default
method.description: Commits the pending masked delta state for [param peer] as of [param sequence], and what an override of [method _sync_note_sent] adds to rather than replaces. A delta is only sound against a baseline the recipient is known to hold, and this is how that baseline moves forward. It moves when a frame goes out rather than when it is acknowledged, so the delta this frame produced is the one the next frame builds on. A session that replicates nothing commits nothing.

method.name: table_admit_frame_default
method.description: The stock verdict on one inbound table frame, and what an override of [method _table_admit_frame] narrows rather than replaces. It takes no route because a table frame is route-0 addressed and the routes it carries are knowable only mid-decode, so everything it judges is in the header. That is who sent it, which table it names, and whether that table's sealed schema agrees. A frame from a peer other than the server is counted as well as rejected, because the count is what separates a rejected sender from a table nobody is publishing. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the frame is admitted ┠╴ERR_INVALID_DATA payload or header is empty, an unimplemented flag is set, or the schema hash disagrees ┠╴ERR_UNAUTHORIZED sender is not the server ┖╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST the header names a table this session does not hold [/codeblock]

method.name: table_commit
method.description: Fixes [param table]'s written routes and columns as the applied state readers compare against. Stamped with the session's own tick, because a commit is what fixes the frame a reader dates itself against and two clocks would date it twice. [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the wave was applied ┠╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST table names nothing valid ┖╴ERR_INVALID_DATA the schema is open, a route wave was never written, a column was not written this wave, or a column's element count disagrees with routes.size() times its declared stride [/codeblock]

method.name: table_create
method.description: A table over [param schema], keyed by the schema's name. Binding a schema whose name already carries a table returns that table, so a script reload finds its own handle rather than creating a second one. An unsealed schema has no address order yet and is rejected.

method.name: table_find
method.description: The handle [method table_create] created for [param name]'s sealed schema, or an invalid [RID] when it has created none.

method.name: table_find_or_adopt
method.description: The table this session bound for [param name], compiling and creating first when the process-wide schema registry has a declaration this session never adopted. The schema sweep runs before the table sweep, because a table is created from a sealed schema. Declare every schema before the session goes online. A table's wire id is its position when the bound tables are sorted by name, so two peers that bound different sets number them differently, and [method table_get_wire_hash] is what catches that. [method schema_find_or_adopt] is the lookup.

method.name: table_get_row
method.description: The row holding [param route] in [param table], or [code]-1[/code] when it is absent.

method.name: table_get_rows
method.description: The row for each entry in [param routes], preserving input order and returning [code]-1[/code] for each absent route.

method.name: table_get_schema
