method.name: transport_cancel_peer_creation
method.description: Withdraws the work [method transport_create_peer] started for [param ticket]. The request settles with one [code](null, ERR_SKIP, "")[/code] callback and no peer is ever offered, and [method NetwTransport._cancel_peer_creation] runs on the provider so it can release whatever it provisionally acquired. Cancellation succeeds until the result is committed. It has no effect after the completion [Callable] starts or for a ticket created by another session. [method transport_unregister] performs the same withdrawal on every unfinished request of the transport it retires, settling those with [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAVAILABLE] instead.

method.name: transport_create_peer
method.description:
Asks [param transport] to build one [MultiplayerPeer] and returns a cancellation ticket. [param mode] picks [constant TRANSPORT_MODE_HOST] or [constant TRANSPORT_MODE_CLIENT], [param address] is what a client joins, and [param settings] is what a host is built from. [param settings] is copied on the way in, nested containers and all, so a caller may reuse the dictionary immediately. [param completed] is called exactly once, in a later frame, as [code]completed(peer: MultiplayerPeer, error: Error, detail: String)[/code]. Success is [code](peer, OK, "")[/code], failure is [code](null, error, detail)[/code], and a cancellation that won the race is [code](null, ERR_SKIP, "")[/code]. [param progress] is optional and is called as [code]progress(step: StringName, message: String, ratio: float)[/code] while the build runs, never after [param completed]. [b]Assign the peer inside the callback, before it returns.[/b] That is the whole window in which the offer can be claimed. The callback must not [code]await[/code] before assigning, must not store the peer to assign later, and must not hand it to another session, which is rejected. Returning without assigning [b]declines[/b] the offer, and the session then closes the peer and releases the provider resources behind it, so an ignored success leaks nothing and owes the caller no release call. A caller that genuinely needs to hold an unassigned peer builds one through its own SDK and assigns it the ordinary way. A successful callback means a peer that can be assigned and nothing more. It is not a connection and not an admitted player. Assigning it starts the connection, [signal MultiplayerAPI.connected_to_server] and [signal MultiplayerAPI.connection_failed] report how that went, and [method session_submit_join] is what admits a player. The result is an invalid [RID] only when [param completed] is not callable or the session is disposed, and no callback happens in that case. Every other rejection, an unheld [param transport] included, returns a valid ticket and one deferred callback carrying the error. The ticket identifies work in flight and nothing else. It has no getters and it retires itself once [param completed] has run, so cancelling a retired, invalid or unknown ticket does nothing. [codeblock] var ticket := api.transport_create_peer( relay, NetwMultiplayer.TRANSPORT_MODE_CLIENT, "eu-1.example.com", {}, _created)
func _created(peer: MultiplayerPeer, error: Error, _detail: String): if error != OK: return api.multiplayer_peer = peer # here, or the offer is declined [/codeblock]

method.name: transport_find
method.description: The handle for the transport that builds peers of [param peer_class], invalid when nothing on this build owns that class. This is the only method here that takes a peer class name. Everything else takes the handle, so a caller spells a class once and holds a handle after. A handle is stable for as long as the transport is installed, so a picker drawn from [method transport_list] can be redrawn without renumbering. [codeblock] var enet := api.transport_find(&"ENetMultiplayerPeer") api.transport_create_peer( enet, NetwMultiplayer.TRANSPORT_MODE_HOST, "", {port = 21253}, assign_it) [/codeblock]

method.name: transport_get_param
method.description: One field of what [param transport] tells a form about itself, named by [param param]. [code]null[/code] when this session holds no such transport, which is also what a handle another session created returns. Returns transport metadata for a host or join form. [constant TRANSPORT_PARAM_CAPABILITIES] returns a [enum TransportCapability] mask. [constant TRANSPORT_PARAM_HOST_SETTINGS] and [constant TRANSPORT_PARAM_CLIENT_SETTINGS] return typed form fields used by [method transport_create_peer]. [codeblock] var caps: int = api.transport_get_param( t, NetwMultiplayer.TRANSPORT_PARAM_CAPABILITIES) if caps & NetwMultiplayer.TRANSPORT_CAN_HOST: show_host_button() [/codeblock]

method.name: transport_list
method.description: Every transport this session can reach, as [RID] handles. The installed ones come first in registration order, then the ones a [LobbyDirectory] registered. A peer of a class nothing lists still works when a game assigns it itself, because this is what a server browser draws rather than what the session admits.

method.name: transport_register
method.description: Registers a [NetwTransport] subclass with this session and returns its handle, keyed by the peer class [method NetwTransport._peer_class] names. [param type] is the [Script] itself rather than an instance, because the session builds one per operation. The handle is invalid when the script names no peer class, and the reason is logged. The registration belongs to the session, not to the process. It is released when the session is disposed, so a project-wide transport is registered in each session's setup path rather than once at load. The stock transports are not registered by anyone and are reachable from every session with no setup at all, which is what keeps the zero-configuration path free of this call. One peer class has one transport per session. Registering the same [param type] returns its existing handle. Registering another script for that peer class fails and returns an invalid handle. Call [method transport_unregister] before replacing it. A registration does hide a stock transport of the same peer class, checked in this order, closest first. - [b]a transport registered on this session[/b] - the stock transport for that peer class - one a [LobbyDirectory] registered [codeblock] func _ready() -> void: var api := Netw.of(self) var relay := api.transport_register(MyRelayTransport) var caps: int = api.transport_get_param( relay, NetwMultiplayer.TRANSPORT_PARAM_CAPABILITIES) [/codeblock]

method.name: transport_unregister
method.description: Withdraws the registration [method transport_register] created, so [param transport] stops being selectable and its handle stops resolving. [constant @GlobalScope.OK] when this session held it, [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST] for a handle this session never created, one already withdrawn, or a stock or directory transport, none of which are a caller's to withdraw. This is not a disconnect. A peer this transport already handed over stays assigned and stays serviced, because a game clears a peer by writing [code]multiplayer_peer = null[/code] and nothing else does. What ends is work that has not delivered a peer yet. A build still in flight settles with [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAVAILABLE] rather than waiting for a transport that is gone, and its listings stop reaching [method endpoint_list]. [codeblock] var relay := api.transport_register(MyRelayTransport) # ... later, when the relay SDK is shut down api.transport_unregister(relay) [/codeblock] [codeblock lang=text] Error ┠╴OK the registration was withdrawn ┖╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST transport was never created here, is already withdrawn, or names a stock or directory transport [/codeblock]

members.member: Whether [member inner] accepts encoded [Object] values when it decodes the arguments of a call it dispatches itself. This session does not extend [SceneMultiplayer], so it inherits none of that class's configuration. It re-declares this one under the engine's own spelling, along with [member server_relay], [member refuse_new_connections], [member max_sync_packet_size], [member max_delta_packet_size], [member root_path], [member auth_callback] and [member auth_timeout], so a game swapping one API for the other finds the same knobs under the same names. That is why these carry no family prefix while the rest of this class does. [member inner]'s own dispatch is reached only for a call [method rpc_call] could not route onto a [NetwEntity]. Networked's own state and action protocols convert an entity or a node to a handle before sending and never encode a raw object, so this flag governs that fallback alone.

The application's own handler for authentication packets, run after Networked has classified its reserved protocol frames. Installing one makes the session authenticate the game's way instead of its own. It then sends no greeting of its own and takes no identity from one.

The [NetwAuthFlow] this session checks arriving peers with, resolved in this order. - a flow installed through [method auth_set_flow] - the flow built by the factory [method Netw.configure_auth] declared - [code]null[/code], and every peer is let in A [code]null[/code] here means open admission only when nothing was declared. A declared factory that failed to build rejects every peer instead.

How long, in seconds, a peer may stay in authentication before the session drops it, with zero meaning no deadline. The value lives on the wrapped [MultiplayerAPI] rather than here, so a session wrapping nothing reads zero and a write goes nowhere. Whatever runs the authentication is what counts the deadline, and a second copy here could disagree with it.

Every connected peer as a roster row, joined or not, in peer order. A row exists from the moment a peer connects. Its join adds a [ResolvedJoin] to that row, which is what moves it into [member participants]. This is the whole roster, including peers that have connected and not yet joined.

The wrapped [SceneMultiplayer]. It owns the [MultiplayerPeer], the connection lifecycle, [method SceneMultiplayer.send_bytes], and the auth protocol, and this session wraps it rather than reimplementing peer transport. Never [code]null[/code]. A session with none assigned makes its own at [code]/root[/code], because an empty root path is an error rather than an unset value. Assigning a new one re-binds everything this session listens to.

Whether this peer holds server authority. A dedicated server, a listen server, and a session with no connection at all all return [code]true[/code]. A session that has connected to nothing is its own authority, which is what lets a single-player game admit its own entities, claim its own routes and create its own scenes with no network, exactly as [MultiplayerSpawner] and [MultiplayerSynchronizer] do. An ended session returns to that state. Authority is withheld the moment a session declares itself something else. [method session_set_role] with [constant ROLE_CLIENT] returns [code]false[/code] before any connection exists, so a client waiting to connect never acts as a server. An authority with no session has no peers, so every broadcast it authorizes reaches nobody. A caller that needs a live hosted session reads [member is_online] as well.

Whether this peer has a player of its own. True at [constant ROLE_CLIENT] and [constant ROLE_LISTEN_SERVER], and false at [constant ROLE_NONE] and [constant ROLE_DEDICATED_SERVER]. A listen server returns [code]true[/code] here and [code]true[/code] to [member is_host] at once, because it is both this session's authority and one of its own players. [member is_host] returns authority and this returns whether a local player exists, and the two questions are independent.

Whether [member state] reads [constant SESSION_STATE_ONLINE], meaning the session carries traffic rather than attempting or leaving a connection. [member is_host] can hold with no live session at all, since a session with no role and no connection is its own authority. A caller that needs a hosted session with peers connected, rather than one merely allowed to act as a server, reads this alongside it.
The accepted [NetwParticipant] for this peer, or [code]null[/code] before its join is accepted.

The entity this peer is represented by, or [code]null[/code] when none represents it. The session holds this entity directly rather than looking it up by route, because retiring an entity has to ask whether that entity is this peer's own, and asking by route returns yes for every entity that has one. A scene change spawns the replacement before retiring the original, so a route-keyed test would drop a local player that had already moved on.

The largest packet [member inner] builds for its delta-compressed state synchronization, carrying [SceneMultiplayer]'s spelling for the reason [member allow_object_decoding] gives. The value lives on [member inner] and is mirrored here rather than held here, so a session that wraps nothing reads zero and a write goes nowhere. Unlike [member max_sync_packet_size] nothing in this session reads it, so it reaches only the wrapped [SceneMultiplayer]'s own delta encoding.

The largest packet [member inner] builds for its own state synchronization, carrying [SceneMultiplayer]'s spelling for the reason [member allow_object_decoding] gives. This is the one of the mirrored properties that this session reads a second time. Networked's own state broadcast sizes its per-tick frames against this value less a fixed headroom for its framing, never below a floor of 128 bytes, so lowering it tightens Networked's own packing as well as the wrapped [SceneMultiplayer]'s. A session that wraps nothing reads zero, which lands that budget on the floor rather than removing the limit.

Every accepted participant known by this peer. A participant appears here once its peer has an accepted [ResolvedJoin], so a connected peer that has not joined yet is absent. [member connected_participants] is the roster row that exists from the moment a peer connects.

Every player entity across every live scene. A player lives inside a scene, so the session reads its players by asking every scene rather than keeping a second roster that could disagree with [method scene_get_players]. Scenes partition the players, so a name is unique across this whole array and never merely within one scene.

Whether [member inner] rejects arriving peer connections, carrying [SceneMultiplayer]'s spelling for the reason [member allow_object_decoding] gives. The flag is only as real as the [MultiplayerPeer] underneath it, and [LocalMultiplayerPeer] does not implement it at all. A session on the in-process loopback reads [code]false[/code] whatever a game writes here, which is why who gets in is decided by [member auth_flow] and the session's own roster rather than by this.

The peer whose call is being dispatched right now, which is what a method called through [method rpc_call] reads to learn who called it. It is read off the session rather than passed as an argument, because a remote method's signature belongs to the game and cannot be widened to carry a sender. [method rpc_call] sets it to this peer around a local dispatch and restores whatever it held afterwards, so a local call nested inside a remote one leaves the outer call reading the right sender. Read-only, because only the dispatch that saves and restores it may move it. A write from outside would make the next call read a sender that never made it.

What this peer is to the session. - [constant ROLE_NONE] no session at all - [constant ROLE_CLIENT] a peer holding no authority - [constant ROLE_DEDICATED_SERVER] authority with no player of its own - [constant ROLE_LISTEN_SERVER] authority held by a peer that plays too [member is_host] and [member is_local_client] are the two questions a caller usually has, and both are read from this. Read-only, because a role is declared through [method session_set_role] and the machine resolves what the session actually became.

The node this session roots relative addressing at, resolved from [member inner]'s [member SceneMultiplayer.root_path] the way the native replicator resolves its own. In every shipped configuration this is the owning [MultiplayerTree], and it stays valid when no tree owns the session. A reader installed through [method session_set_root] returns instead, which is how an embedding that resolves its root differently keeps one result for both.

The path [member inner] resolves a node reference against, carrying [SceneMultiplayer]'s spelling for the reason [member allow_object_decoding] gives. [member root] is the node this path resolves to, and [method session_is_active] returns by comparing the session the [SceneTree] holds at this path against this one, so moving the path moves which registration this session claims to be. A session that wraps nothing reads an empty [NodePath] and a write goes nowhere.

Whether [member inner] relays traffic between clients through the server rather than letting them address each other directly, carrying [SceneMultiplayer]'s spelling for the reason [member allow_object_decoding] gives. The value lives on [member inner] and is mirrored here rather than held here, so a session that wraps nothing reads [code]false[/code] and a write goes nowhere. Nothing in this session reads it a second time, so relaying is exactly what the wrapped [SceneMultiplayer] decides.

Where this session is in its life. - [constant SESSION_STATE_OFFLINE] nothing connected and nothing sought - [constant SESSION_STATE_CONNECTING] a host or join in flight, may fail - [constant SESSION_STATE_ONLINE] carrying traffic - [constant SESSION_STATE_DISCONNECTING] tearing down, admitting nothing new [member is_online] is the shorthand for the reading most callers want.

signal.name: clock_after_tick
signal.description: Announced by the session clock at the end of each tick, after game logic. The clock announces on the session rather than on itself, so a consumer holding the session never has to hold the clock and there is one place a tick can be subscribed to.

signal.name: clock_after_tick_loop
signal.description: Announced by the session clock once after [method clock_physics_step]'s tick loop finishes, whether or not it ran a tick. Not announced by [method clock_step], which is a step rather than a frame.

signal.name: clock_before_tick
signal.description: Announced by the session clock at the start of each tick, before game logic.

signal.name: clock_before_tick_loop
signal.description: Announced by the session clock once before [method clock_physics_step]'s tick loop runs, whether or not it will run a tick. Not announced by [method clock_step], which is a step rather than a frame.

signal.name: clock_configured
signal.description: Announced once, after this session consumed its clock configuration and armed the automatic pump. A listener connected afterwards has already missed it and reads [method clock_is_configured] instead.

signal.name: clock_on_tick
signal.description: Announced by the session clock during each tick. Primary simulation logic subscribes here.

signal.name: clock_pong_received
signal.description: Announced by [method clock_ingest_pong] once a round trip [method clock_send_ping] opened has closed and the clock has calibrated against it. [param data] is that sample, which is the only place the raw round trip is readable at all. [codeblock lang=text] Dictionary ┠╴rtt_raw float this sample's round trip, in seconds ┠╴rtt_avg float the running average round trip ┠╴rtt_jitter float the running jitter estimate ┠╴diff int ticks the calibration moved this peer ┠╴tick int the tick after calibrating ┠╴display_offset float the offset the display is running ┠╴recommended_display_offset float the offset this sample recommends ┠╴is_stable bool whether jitter is under threshold ┖╴is_synchronized bool whether a calibration has ever landed [/codeblock] [signal clock_stability_changed] and [signal clock_synchronized] announce the transitions of the last two, so a listener that only wants those does not read this at all.

signal.name: clock_stability_changed
signal.description: Announced by the session clock when [method clock_is_stable] flips, so a listener sees the transition rather than having to poll for it.

signal.name: clock_synchronized
signal.description: Announced by the session clock once, when its first calibration lands. A later pong recalibrates without re-announcing.

signal.name: clock_tickrate_mismatch
signal.description: Announced when a handshake reply reports a tickrate this session does not run and [method clock_set_mismatch_action] holds [constant MISMATCH_ACTION_SIGNAL], which is the setting that hands the decision to the game instead of taking one. [param peer_id] is the peer that replied and [param their_tickrate] is the rate it reported. Neither other action announces it. [constant MISMATCH_ACTION_WARN] only logs the mismatch, and [constant MISMATCH_ACTION_DISCONNECT] closes the peer.

signal.name: embed_phase_changed
signal.description: Emitted when [method embed_phase] advances, carrying the phase just entered. The installing embedding is the only caller that advances it, through [method embed_settle].

signal.name: endpoint_added
signal.description: A row entered [method endpoint_list]. A row already known announces nothing, because its key is the pair it always was.

signal.name: endpoint_removed
signal.description: A row left [method endpoint_list].

signal.name: endpoint_updated
signal.description: A probe or a listing returned for this row. What changed is read back through [method endpoint_get_param] and [method endpoint_get_state], so a browser redraws one row rather than the list.

signal.name: entity_dead
signal.description: Emitted once when this session learns that [param route] has ended. The route reads [constant ENTITY_STATE_DEAD], its body services are released, and the wrapper has already left the live index, so [method entity_get_view] returns [code]null[/code] for [param route] here and for the rest of the cycle. A materialized entity emits [signal NetwEntity.despawned] before this, and that per-entity completion is what a tracked entity with no route gets instead. A move emits neither, and a receiving peer that lost only its copy emits [signal entity_hidden].

signal.name: entity_hidden
signal.description: Emitted when this receiving peer loses its copy of [param route], carrying the old [NetwEntity] as [param entity]. The route reads [constant ENTITY_STATE_ABSENT] afterwards and the entity has already left the live set, exactly as for [signal entity_dead]. What survives is the identity and anything waiting on it, so a later spawn from the server binds the same handle to a new node. Listen to this rather than [signal entity_dead] for anything that should come back. [signal NetwEntity.hidden] fires first and carries what was released. A hide the server issued reports before the old node is freed, and a copy this peer deleted itself reports once that node is already gone. Neither changes the server's scene admission, and neither emits[signal entity_dead].

signal.name: entity_lingering
signal.description: Emitted when an entity enters [constant ENTITY_STATE_LINGERING]. Its [NetwEntity] stays resolvable, because a lingering entity has not gone yet.

signal.name: entity_live
signal.description: Emitted when a route becomes live. It carries the [NetwEntity] the session itself holds, so a listener resolves the same object the session will return with for the rest of that route's life.

signal.name: lagcomp_action_gate_fallback
signal.description: Announced when an action timed [constant NetwAction.TIMING_TICK_ALIGNED_STATE_READY] reaches [member NetwLagCompensationConfig.input_gate_deadline_ticks] without the input state it was waiting for, and so executes best effort rather than waiting further. [param key] is the action's key and [param view_tick] the tick it was aligned to. An action the gate admits on time is not announced, and every announcement is also counted into [method lagcomp_metrics]'s [code]gate_fallbacks[/code].

signal.name: participant_joined
signal.description: Emitted for every peer the session admits, this one included. A peer with no roster row has not been admitted and is never announced.

signal.name: participant_local_joined
signal.description: Emitted when the peer being admitted is this one, ahead of [signal participant_joined], so a listener handling both sees itself arrive before it sees the roster grow.

signal.name: participant_viewport_changed
signal.description: Emitted when [method scene_participant_viewport] resolves to a different [SubViewport], and [param viewport] is [code]null[/code] when it resolves to none. A settle that lands on what the last one did stays silent, so a listener is never told to re-adopt a display it already holds. The settle is deferred, because the local player is assigned while its entity is still entering the tree and the viewport it lands in resolves only once that entry finishes.

signal.name: peer_authenticating
signal.description: Republishes [signal SceneMultiplayer.peer_authenticating] from the transport this session holds. A transport the session replaces stops republishing at once.

signal.name: peer_authentication_failed
signal.description: Republishes [signal SceneMultiplayer.peer_authentication_failed] from the transport this session holds, after recording the rejection as a [code]PEER_AUTH_FAILED[/code] event, so a sink reads it in the order the session decided it.

signal.name: peer_kick_requested
signal.description: Emitted when a client asks for a peer to be kicked. Heard only by a session holding peer id 1. A request that does not carry a target and a reason is dropped rather than announced against a default target.

signal.name: peer_kicked
signal.description: Emitted when server authority kicks this peer, before the connection closes. A notice from anyone but the server is dropped.

signal.name: peer_packet
signal.description: Emitted for a datagram this session did not frame, so a game's own byte traffic reaches it over the same transport. A datagram that is this session's own and cannot be read is never announced here.

signal.name: predict_owner_divergence
signal.description: Announced on server authority when an owner's claimed post-state for a transition disagrees with the state authority itself reached, so a diagnostic sink hears the disagreement the tick it is judged rather than reading a counter later. [param peer] is the controller of the entity seated in the slot, [param entry] is the transition judged, and [param attribution] is the [enum NetwPredictJournal.Attribution] the comparison charged the divergence to. A claim that matched is counted and not announced, and so is one the comparison could charge to nothing, which leaves [constant NetwPredictJournal.UNKNOWN] out of this signal's vocabulary. Both are counted either way, through [member NetwPredictStats.client_fp_verified] and [member NetwPredictStats.client_mismatches].

signal.name: scene_activated
signal.description: Emitted by [method scene_activate] for the container a caller made current, once per activation and never for a rejection. Reusing a container that was already live still announces, because the signal reports what the session now presents and not whether a spawn happened.

signal.name: scene_despawned
signal.description: Emitted for a scene the session has dropped, after its rows are gone and everything waiting on the change has run, so a listener reading membership sees the session without it. Dropping a node the session never held still announces, because the scene leaving is the fact being reported and having nothing to drop is not a rejection.

signal.name: scene_entity_moved
signal.description: Emitted for a move that completed, after the mover's membership and saved rows have settled and before the move's [NetwPromise] resolves, so a listener and an awaiting caller read the same session. A rejected move never arrives and is never announced.

signal.name: scene_live
signal.description: Emitted for the scene a newly live route belongs to. The handle is the scene's own, so a node coming live inside a scene announces the scene and not itself.

signal.name: scene_local_changed
signal.description: Republishes the scene change of the participant this session decided is the local peer, bound when that row joins and released when the roster drops it. Another peer changing scene is not this session changing scene. A participant raises its own [code]scene_changed[/code] when the session takes or empties its seat while admitting or releasing it. A seat never moves on its own, so a game calls [method scene_admit] and [method scene_release] and the seat follows.

signal.name: scene_local_player_changed
signal.description: Emitted when the entity representing this peer changes, including to [code]null[/code] when the route carrying it retires. Decided where a route goes live, because that is the only moment the result can change, and read off the entity's own record rather than through the wrapper. A session with no transport represents nobody, which an offline session returning unique id 1 would otherwise look like.

signal.name: scene_spawned
signal.description: Emitted once for each scene the session takes in. It fires before any player has been admitted, so a listener reads the scene and not yet who is in it. A scene the session rejected to take in announces nothing.

signal.name: scene_startup_spawned
signal.description: Emitted once server authority enters the session. It reports that startup finished rather than that anything spawned, so a session with nothing to spawn still announces and a listener waiting on it never waits forever.

signal.name: service_registered
signal.description: Emitted whenever a service is registered, whether through [method service_register] or through [method Netw.service_register]. Registering the same instance again does nothing and announces nothing.

signal.name: service_unregistered
signal.description: Emitted by [method service_unregister], and only when the type still names that service, so a service already replaced cannot unregister the one that replaced it.

signal.name: session_disconnect_requested
signal.description: Emitted when a client asks to leave. Heard only by a session holding peer id 1, and [param peer_id] is who actually sent the request rather than anything the request claims.

signal.name: session_ended
signal.description: Emitted on leaving [constant SESSION_STATE_ONLINE], so a session that failed before it ever connected never announces an ending.

signal.name: session_entered
signal.description: Announced by the session machine on reaching [constant SESSION_STATE_ONLINE].

signal.name: session_join_failed
signal.description: This peer's own join was rejected and no player was seated for it. A game connects through [signal NetwConnectHandle.join_failed] on [method Netw.connection] rather than here.

signal.name: session_join_submitted
signal.description: Emitted immediately before [param username] and [param args] go out, whether they travel to a server or are delivered to this session itself. This announces that the join was sent and never that it was accepted. A server that rejects it announced this first.

signal.name: session_poll_started
signal.description: Emitted at the start of each session poll. [param delta] is the wall-clock gap since the previous one, and zero on the session's first.

signal.name: session_reclaimed
signal.description: Announced immediately after [signal session_ended], so every listener of that signal has returned before this one fires. It is the phase, not a second ending. A listener that frees nodes the session owns binds here rather than on [signal session_ended], which is what keeps a listener of the announcement from being handed a node another listener already freed.

signal.name: session_server_disconnecting
signal.description: Emitted when the server announces it is going away. A notice from anyone but the server is dropped.

signal.name: session_state_changed
signal.description: Announced by the session machine on every legal edge. An edge it rejects is not a transition, so it is not published.

signal.name: session_tree_paused
signal.description: Emitted when server authority pauses the session. Pausing the engine is something a listener does in response rather than part of the decision, so the session announces this once and everything that reacts reads the same announcement. A notice from anyone but the server is dropped.

signal.name: session_tree_unpaused
signal.description: The twin of [signal session_tree_paused].

signal.name: table_received
signal.description: Emitted once for each table a commit produced or an arriving frame touched. [param tick] is the one the commit stamped, so several commits inside one tick collapse to the last.

constants.constant: An entity's record moved to its live stage outside a reparent and the wrapper is about to emit its own spawning signal. Belongs to the lifecycle group. detail is empty, and entity_id and peer both name the entity settling.
An entity's route finished binding and the entity is live. Belongs to the lifecycle group. detail is empty, and entity_id and peer both name the entity that just went live.

An entity's despawn began. Belongs to the lifecycle group. detail carries {reason}, and model carries {entity_id, peer_id}, which the terminal [constant EVENT_DESPAWNED] row for the same route reuses since it carries none of its own.

An entity finished despawning and its route is retired. It is terminal, so its own entity_id is empty and its model is instead whatever the last non-empty model recorded for the route held, ordinarily [constant EVENT_DESPAWNING]'s {entity_id, peer_id}.
An entity was reparented. Belongs to the lifecycle group. detail carries {reason, moved}, where moved is true when the reparent also carried a target global position.
An entity's lifecycle stage changed. Belongs to the lifecycle group. detail carries {from, to}, the stage values on either side of the transition.
An entity's controlling peer changed. Belongs to the lifecycle group. detail carries {from, to}, and peer is the newly assigned controller.

A peer asked to take control of an entity. Belongs to the lifecycle group. detail carries {requester}, peer is the requester, and verdict is OK when authority granted control or an unauthorized error when it rejected.
An entity was hidden from its observers without being despawned. Belongs to the lifecycle group. detail is empty.
A peer began seeing an entity through one layer. Belongs to the interest group. detail carries {layer}, and peer is the one that began seeing it.
A peer stopped seeing an entity through one layer. Belongs to the interest group. detail carries {layer}, and peer is the one that stopped seeing it.

A peer began observing an entity through an awareness edge that is not a layer edge, and the entity's own observer_entered signal fires alongside it. Belongs to the interest group. detail carries {layer}, and peer is the observer.

A peer stopped observing an entity through an awareness edge that is not a layer edge, and the entity's own observer_left signal fires alongside it. Belongs to the interest group. detail carries {layer}, and peer is the observer.

A pending interest recompute was applied and observers were refreshed for the tick. Belongs to the interest group. detail is empty, and route is 0 because it reports the commit as a whole rather than one entity.
A prediction episode opened for an entity's slot. Belongs to the prediction group. detail carries {transition, attribution}, and model carries the full episode record the slot held at that moment.

A prediction episode closed for an entity's slot. Belongs to the prediction group. detail carries {transition, attribution} merged with the episode's disposition fields, and model carries the full episode record.

A slot's prediction demoted into fallback after a breach it could not absorb. Belongs to the prediction group. detail carries {transition, attribution, demoted}, and model carries the full episode record.
A slot drove a new predicted transition. Belongs to the prediction group. detail carries {transition, label, kind, fresh}, and the row is only raised when the drive actually produced a transition.
A slot consumed a buffered predicted input. Belongs to the prediction group. detail carries {depth, buffer, action}.
A slot's prediction was judged against the authoritative state it received. Belongs to the prediction group. detail carries {transition, divergence, corrected}.
A slot applied a recovery plan after a divergence. Belongs to the prediction group. detail carries {transition, skip, teleport}.

A slot's prediction diverged from the authoritative state by more than its tolerance, and the handle's own divergence_detected signal fires alongside it. Belongs to the prediction group. detail carries {transition, attribution, divergence}.

A slot corrected its predicted state after a divergence, and the handle's own recovered signal fires alongside it. Belongs to the prediction group. detail carries {transition, attribution, teleport, moved}, where moved is the dictionary of properties the correction actually wrote.
An inbound sync frame, on the sync, row, row-delta, row-window or delta channel, passed or failed admission. Belongs to the gates group. detail is empty, and verdict is what the session returned.
An inbound spawn frame passed or failed admission. Belongs to the gates group. detail is empty, route is 0 since spawn admission is not per-entity, and verdict is what the session returned.
An inbound table frame passed or failed admission. Belongs to the gates group. detail is empty, route is 0, and verdict is what the session returned.
An inbound prediction frame, command, ack, relay or relay request, passed or failed admission. Belongs to the gates group. detail is empty, and verdict is what the session returned.
A sync frame finished encoding for a peer. Belongs to the stages group. detail carries {bytes}, the encoded size, and peer is the recipient.
A sync frame finished decoding for an entity's component. Belongs to the stages group. detail carries {comp}, and verdict is what decoding returned.
A deferred send pass gathered row offers into outbound sends. Belongs to the stages group. detail carries {offers, sends}, the offers considered and the sends actually produced.
A batch of received frames finished applying. Belongs to the stages group. detail carries {frames}, the frame count, peer is the sender, and verdict is the worst error the batch produced, or OK.
An entity was declared for spawning. Belongs to the stages group. detail is empty, route is the declared entity's route, and verdict is what the session returned.

The spawn planner reconciled the roster against connected peers. Belongs to the stages group. detail is empty, route is 0, and verdict is an unconfigured error when the planner produced no plan, or OK.
The spawn pipeline finished constructing an entity's node. Belongs to the stages group. detail carries {built}, whether construction actually produced a node.
A display track recorded a value for a tick. Belongs to the stages group. detail carries {track, tick}.
A display runtime pumped its interpolation. Belongs to the stages group. detail carries {tick}, the display tick it pumped to.
A display track wrote a value onto an entity. Belongs to the stages group. detail carries {track}, and verdict is what [method _display_write] returned.

A table finished committing its dirty rows for a tick. Belongs to the stages group. detail carries {stage, rows}, where stage is always "table" and rows is the committed row count, and verdict is what the commit returned.

A rejection was counted toward what [method stats_get_verdict_count] returns. Belongs to the verdicts group. detail carries {stage, counted}, where stage is always "gate" and counted says whether the session actually recorded it, and verdict is the error being counted.

An override point a game replaced returned something the session cannot use, so the default result stood. Belongs to the verdicts group. detail carries {seam, stage, reason}, and verdict is always an invalid-data error.
Belongs to the session group and names a session state transition. Nothing in the session emits it yet, so no detail shape is established for it, and a watcher should not assume one.
A peer connected to the session. Belongs to the session group. detail carries {peer}, route is 0, and peer names the peer that connected.
A peer disconnected from the session. Belongs to the session group. detail carries {peer}, route is 0, and peer names the peer that disconnected.
A peer failed authentication. Belongs to the session group. detail carries {peer}, and peer names the peer that was rejected.
A scene container went live for a route. Belongs to the session group. detail carries {scene}, the scene's name.
A carrier datagram was sent to a peer. Belongs to the carrier group. detail carries {size, seq, reliable}, and peer is the recipient.
A carrier datagram was received from a peer. Belongs to the carrier group. detail carries {size, seq, reliable}, where seq is -1 for a reliable datagram, and peer is the sender.
A carrier datagram from a peer failed to parse as a known frame. Belongs to the carrier group. detail carries {size}, peer is the sender, and verdict is always an invalid-data error.
A peer's acknowledged sequence advanced. Belongs to the carrier group. detail carries {ack}, the newly acknowledged sequence, and peer is the peer whose ack moved.
The row was recorded before the act it names ran, so what it reports is an intention rather than an outcome and no verdict on it is settled yet. Only an act the session announces twice emits one.

The row was recorded once the act it names had run, which is what an event row is unless it says otherwise. A sink counting acts counts this phase and ignores [constant EVENT_PHASE_BEFORE], or it counts the announced ones twice.

The first byte of a reliable Networked datagram. Game packets sent through this session must not start with this byte or either magic value below. The receiver uses the first byte to detect Networked framing. Invalid Networked frames are rejected as malformed.
The first byte of an unreliable Networked datagram, which carries a per-peer sequence. See [constant CARRIER_MAGIC_RELIABLE].
The first byte of an unreliable Networked datagram that also echoes the freshest inbound sequence and the delivery history behind it. See [constant CARRIER_MAGIC_RELIABLE].

[bool]. Whether commits ride the reliable lane, passed to [method table_set_param]. A table that changes rarely wants this, because it has no next commit to heal a lost datagram with, and a table published every tick does not. Table params are local configuration rather than wire surface, so one never enters [method table_get_wire_hash] and a later value is not a wire event.
The move is rejected because its source or destination is not live.
The mover already belongs to the destination.
The server's own truth, authored by it and kept in a rewind timeline. A body pose is the usual example.
A client's claim, sent to the server only and verified by it, also kept for rewind. Movement keys are the usual example.
Trusted display sent to everyone, checked by nobody and kept nowhere. An aim arrow is the usual example.

The route was never issued, or was issued by a peer this one has not heard from. [enum EntityState] is what this peer knows about a route, and nothing else knows it for them. The four values are ordered and a route only moves forward through them, so a route that is dead never comes back to life. Whether this peer can see the entity is a separate question, and a route may reach [constant ENTITY_STATE_ABSENT] and return without spending a life.
The entity exists and accepts traffic.
Despawn has begun. Frames still in flight are dropped rather than treated as addressing nothing.
The route is retired and will not be reissued. Losing sight of an entity is not this, and reads [constant ENTITY_STATE_ABSENT] instead.

This peer holds no copy of the route right now and could be shown one again. Only a receiving peer reaches this, because the server never loses sight of its own entities. It ranks alongside [constant ENTITY_STATE_LIVE] rather than past it. The route keeps naming the same entity, returning costs nothing, and a real despawn still retires it. See [signal entity_hidden] and [constant LEAVE_POLICY_HIDE].
Only members of the layer see its entities. The usual choice for a team or a private room.
Only non-members see its entities. The usual choice for something a player should not see their own copy of.

Scripts declare through the [code skip-lint]Netw.configure_*[/code] family, and a stock [MultiplayerSpawner] or [MultiplayerSynchronizer] arrives through [method MultiplayerAPI.object_configuration_add]. Nothing acts on either yet, and authoring is only in contract here. A [NetwSessionConfig], [NetwClockConfig] or [NetwLagCompensationConfig] pushed through that door is rejected in every phase, because those three are declared once and consumed once. [enum EmbedPhase] says how far a session has come in starting up, and [member state] says whether it is connected. The two are separate questions and a session returns both at once.
The embedding signalled the authored world is loaded, and the session resolves the winning declarations as one ordered step.
Every declaration has resolved and the session may now host or join. A session reaches here through [method embed_settle] and never leaves.

Tell the peer it no longer holds a copy. The copy is freed, the route reads [constant ENTITY_STATE_ABSENT] on that peer, and a later admission binds the same identity again. This is not a despawn, because an entity a peer stops seeing has not stopped existing.
Keep the copy and stop updating it. It resumes from a stale pose when interest returns, with no spawn cost.
Neither. The game decides, through the layer's own handler.

Hide the copy that was kept, so it stops being drawn where it was last seen. [enum LeavePolicy] decides whether the copy is kept at all, and [enum PerceptionPolicy] decides whether a kept copy is drawn.
Keep drawing the retained copy at its last known pose. A [constant LEAVE_POLICY_RETAIN] entity is still present, so something must say whether it is drawn.
Neither. The game decides, through the layer's own handler.
Resolve from [NetwEntity] control and [member Node.multiplayer_authority]. The default, and correct for almost every entity.
Interpolate replicated snapshots. What a peer uses for somebody else's entity.
Follow the locally predicted body. What a player uses for their own entity.
No smoothing. The node is left alone for the game to drive.
Sample the locally authored simulation each tick and play it back, so the server sees its own world smoothed the same way.
No pump has been chosen yet. A runtime starts here and resolves to one of the other values the first time its role is settled.
Nothing is pumped. Matches [constant DISPLAY_ROLE_DISABLED] and the unresolved [constant DISPLAY_ROLE_AUTO] case, where the node is left for the game to drive.
Sample the recorded history along the session's display timeline, [constant TIMELINE_MODE_BUFFERED] or [constant TIMELINE_MODE_FORECAST]. What [constant DISPLAY_ROLE_REMOTE] pumps.

Sample the recorded history bracketed between the previous and current tick, one tick behind. What [constant DISPLAY_ROLE_AUTHORITY] always pumps, and what [constant DISPLAY_ROLE_PREDICTED] pumps under [constant PREDICTED_MODE_BRACKETED].
Ease the visual toward the live predicted body every frame instead of sampling history. What [constant DISPLAY_ROLE_PREDICTED] pumps under [constant PREDICTED_MODE_CHASE].
Ease the visual toward the live predicted body every frame. Most responsive, and shows correction ripple.
Interpolate between the previous and current tick samples. Steadier, and one tick behind.
Render behind the newest sample by the jitter buffer, always a delayed truth. The default, and the only mode the server ever resolves.

Project along the last replicated velocity, trading buffer delay for extrapolation error. Collision blind, so a body projected toward a wall penetrates it until the bounce sample arrives. Prefer [constant TIMELINE_MODE_BUFFERED] for anything that meets world geometry.

Jump the local tick straight to the measured target on every sample. The local tick is always driven back toward the server's, and this only decides whether that happens in one step or is spread across frames.
Nudge the tick accumulator toward the target, snapping only once the divergence exceeds the configured panic threshold.
Log the tickrate difference and carry on. The default, because a tickrate difference is a configuration mistake rather than a protocol violation.
Close the peer. Choose this only when a mismatched peer cannot be allowed to simulate at all, because it gives the game no way to say what happened.
Emit [signal clock_tickrate_mismatch] and leave the decision to the game. Choose this when the game wants to show the mismatch before deciding.
The layer's [enum LayerPolicy], which composes its viewer set. Layer params are passed to [method interest_layer_set_param].
The layer's [enum LeavePolicy], which decides what happens on the wire when the layer stops admitting an entity.
The layer's [enum PerceptionPolicy], which decides what the local player sees when the layer stops admitting an entity.
[StringName] class of the peer this transport builds, which is the name [method transport_find] takes. Transport params are read through [method transport_get_param].
[String] to call this transport in a picker.
[String] to title the address field with, such as an IP for [ENetMultiplayerPeer], a URL for a WebSocket, or a room id for WebRTC.
[String] to show in the empty address field.
[String] sentence under the address field, empty when it needs none.
[int] mask of [enum TransportCapability], saying what this transport can do on this build and platform.

[Dictionary] describing the fields a host form asks for, one entry per field, typed by its own value. It is what [method transport_create_peer] reads back, and a game that builds its own peer never sees it.
[Dictionary] describing the join form fields. It has the same shape as [constant TRANSPORT_PARAM_HOST_SETTINGS]. Shared fields, such as an ENet [code]port[/code], appear in both dictionaries.
The transport reports itself usable on this build. A picker greys out a row that does not.
This build can listen over this transport at all, which is how a web build stops offering to host.
A row of this transport can be asked what is there without joining it, which is what [method endpoint_probe] needs.
The transport lists what it can reach, which is what [method endpoint_refresh] asks of it.
An empty address means something to this transport, which lets an Add form accept a blank field for a transport that finds its own host.
The transport that builds peers for this row, as a [RID] handle. Read only, because a row is the pairing of a transport with an address and changing either makes a different row.
The address this row reaches, as the transport spells it. Read only, for the reason above.
What a server browser draws for this row. The only field [method endpoint_set_param] will write.
The row's flags, as a bitmask of [constant ENDPOINT_FLAG_CALLER], [constant ENDPOINT_FLAG_AVAILABLE] and [constant ENDPOINT_FLAG_OBSERVED].
What the last probe returned, as an [enum @GlobalScope.Error]. It reads [constant @GlobalScope.FAILED] before anything has probed the row, which is not the same as a probe that failed.
The [NetwServerInfo] the last probe reply carried, or [code]null[/code] when nothing has returned.
The row was added by a caller through [method endpoint_add] rather than found by a listing.
The last probe reached a server that returned.
The row was seen in a listing rather than named by a caller. A row can carry this and [constant ENDPOINT_FLAG_CALLER] at once.

[StringName] naming what kind of scene this is. Two live copies of one arena share the name, because a scene is identified by its [RID]. See [member NetwEntity.scene_label]. Every [enum SceneParam] is read and written through [method scene_get_param] and [method scene_set_param].
The scene's [enum SceneIsolation]. Write-once before the entity arms, because it chooses the container every peer builds.
[bool] gating whether the scene's subtree processes. Freeze and resume.

A participant was admitted or released, and [code]subject[/code] is its peer id. Every [method scene_observe] callback takes [code](present: bool, subject: Variant)[/code], so one registration hears both directions and a caller that only wants arrivals ignores the rest.
A player entity entered or left, and [code]subject[/code] is its entity RID.
Any tracked entity entered or left, and [code]subject[/code] is its entity RID. Players report here too, so a caller wanting only them reads [constant SCENE_EVENT_PLAYER] instead.
Every participant converges on the destination and every other live scene retires. Isolation, the number of live scenes, and whether authority also holds a local player do not change what this means.

One participant travels with the player entities it is enrolled in, and every world keeps running. A change at this scope with no participant to resolve is rejected rather than widened to the session.
The occupants of the caller's own world travel and that world retires, leaving other worlds untouched. A change at this scope with no source world to resolve is rejected.

The scene shares the session's world and its root is a plain [Node]. Each scene chooses its own isolation, so one session can hold a shared lobby and several isolated match worlds at once. It is decided before the scene spawns. Every peer builds the root from the same recipe, and a peer that built the wrong kind has nothing to hang the scene's children on.

A hosting peer builds the scene an offscreen [SubViewport] with its own world, so two live scenes never share a physics space. A peer that only views the scene still builds a plain [Node], because only the host simulates.

How many simulation ticks run per second, as an [int]. The one clock value that must be identical on every peer, so [method clock_set_param] rejects it with [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAUTHORIZED] and a declared [NetwClockConfig] is its only door.
Which correction shape calibration takes, as one of [enum SyncMode].
Seconds between the pings that refresh the round-trip estimate, as a [float].
The most ticks one frame may run, as an [int]. It is a ceiling rather than a target, and the time a capped frame could not spend is kept for the next one.
The frame length above which a frame is read as a hitch rather than as simulated time, in seconds, as a [float]. Crossing it resets the accumulator.
The divergence in ticks above which [constant SYNC_MODE_STRETCH] gives up and snaps, as an [int]. Past it the gap is a desync rather than drift.
The fraction of the remaining divergence [constant SYNC_MODE_STRETCH] closes each frame, as a [float].
How many ticks the display trails the simulation, as an [int]. The buffer the smoothing spends.
The explicit margin, in ticks, the calibration target is placed ahead of the server's own position, as a [float].
How strongly measured jitter widens [constant CLOCK_MONITOR_RECOMMENDED_DISPLAY_OFFSET], as a [float].
How many recent round-trip samples the average and the jitter are taken over, as an [int].
The jitter below which the link counts as stable, in seconds, as a [float]. What [method clock_is_stable] compares against.
Whether the tick factor tracks the physics interpolation fraction, as a [bool].
Whether average drift is logged over rolling windows, as a [bool].
Whether the schedule ignores frame pumps so a rig can own it, as a [bool]. What a deterministic stepper holds while it drives.
A fixed value for [constant CLOCK_MONITOR_TICK_FACTOR] in place of the measured one, as a [float]. Negative restores the measurement.
The most recent round-trip time, in seconds.
The round-trip time averaged over [constant CLOCK_PARAM_JITTER_WINDOW] samples, in seconds.
The spread of those samples, in seconds.
Half of [constant CLOCK_MONITOR_RTT_AVG], in seconds.
One tick's worth of simulated time, in seconds, which is one divided by [constant CLOCK_PARAM_TICKRATE].
How far the current frame has advanced between the last tick and the next, from zero to one.
Where the clock sits inside the current tick, from zero to one. What a pong carries so a calibration target can be a continuous position rather than a whole tick.
The frame time banked toward the next tick, in seconds.
Physics frames per tick, unrounded. [method clock_get_physics_steps_per_tick] is this as a whole number.
The display offset the measured jitter suggests, in ticks. It is a recommendation, and [constant CLOCK_PARAM_DISPLAY_OFFSET] is what the clock actually uses.
How many physics frames this process has run since the clock started counting.
How many session polls it has run over the same span.
The wall-clock seconds that span covers.
[constant CLOCK_MONITOR_PHYSICS_FRAMES] over [constant CLOCK_MONITOR_WALL_SECONDS]. What the engine actually delivered, which is how a starved host is told apart from a mistuned one.
[constant CLOCK_MONITOR_POLLS] over [constant CLOCK_MONITOR_WALL_SECONDS].

[enum DisplayRole]. How the entity is drawn. This is the only one most games ever set, and it is usually left at [constant DISPLAY_ROLE_AUTO]. Every [enum DisplayParam] is read and written through [method display_get_param] and [method display_set_param], and the note after each name is the [Variant] type it takes. [NetwDisplayHandle] publishes twelve of them as named members. [constant DISPLAY_PARAM_MAX_FORECAST_TICKS] and [constant DISPLAY_PARAM_CHASE_GLIDE_TIME] are reached through these two methods only.
[enum PredictedMode]. How a predicted entity turns its body into a pose.
[float] seconds. How long a predicted visual takes to absorb a correction.
[float] seconds. How long [constant PREDICTED_MODE_CHASE] takes to close the gap to the live body.
[enum TimelineMode]. Where on the timeline a remote entity renders.
[int] ticks. How far [constant TIMELINE_MODE_FORECAST] may project past the newest sample before it gives up and holds.
[bool]. Whether the buffer may stretch playback to ride out jitter instead of starving.
[float] as a fraction of normal speed. The ceiling on that stretch.
[float]. How quickly the buffer re-targets when the measured lag moves. Higher follows the network faster and jitters more.
[float]. How much the buffer grows after a starvation, buying margin at the cost of latency.
[float]. Smoothing applied to the buffer floor so it settles rather than chases every sample.
[int] frames. How many starved frames pass before the runtime treats the stream as genuinely stalled.
[int] ticks. How often display tracing samples, or [code]0[/code] to trace nothing.

[int] component id, or the [NodePath] itself. Names the node the smoothed pose is written to. A component id resolves through [method display_set_target_item]. A [NodePath] is stored as written, which is what lets a visual be named before the node exists.

[enum NetwPredict.Archetype]. What the entity starts from, such as a character or a vehicle. Set this first and adjust afterwards. Every [enum PredictParam] is read and written through [method predict_get_param] and [method predict_set_param], writes the like-named member on the entity's [NetwPredictionHandle], and takes the [Variant] type named after it below. An archetype sets most of the rest, so a game usually writes one or two.
[enum NetwPredict.Schedule]. When in the tick the entity simulates.
[enum NetwPredict.MissingInput]. What authority does for a tick whose input never arrived.
[enum NetwPredict.RecoveryPolicy]. What the owner does about a divergence, from replaying it to merely reporting it.
[enum NetwPredict.RestoreMode]. Whether a snap restores to the acknowledged state or extrapolates it forward to now.
[enum NetwPredict.CorrectionMode]. The mechanism a recovery policy is carried out by.
[float] in the property's own units. The fallback distance past which a body is judged to hold nothing worth keeping, used for any property that declares no threshold of its own.
[float]. The tolerance a divergence is judged against wherever the transition was not declared exactly reproducible.
[enum NetwPredict.BreachResponse]. What happens when a client's claimed state cannot be reconciled at all.
[int] ticks. The cap on how far an extrapolated restore may project, so a backlogged acknowledgement cannot launch the body down a long straight line off a curved path.
[int] ticks. How long after a contact the entity stays out of partial recovery, since a body still being disturbed cannot say which properties are safe to leave behind.
[int]. The ceiling on transitions authority replays in one tick, which bounds catch-up cost after a stall.
[int] ticks. How far behind authority may fall before it stops trying to catch up transition by transition.
[int] ticks. The queue depth authority holds before replaying, the [code]buffer[/code] of [method predict_consume]. Zero by default, so the ordinary verdict is simply whether anything is queued.
[int]. How many transitions the owner keeps for replay, which bounds how far a correction can rewind.

[bool]. Whether the island admits approximate agreement rather than demanding reproducible transitions. An island is the set of entities that must be resimulated together because they interact. Its settings are written through [method predict_island_set_param], and [method predict_island_add] is what puts an entity in one.
[bool]. Whether the island claims its transitions are exactly reproducible, which is what entitles them to be judged without tolerance.
[enum NetwPredict.Reconcile]. How the island resimulates after a divergence.
[enum NetwPredict.Promotion]. What causes a nearby entity to be drawn into the island.
[int]. The number of nearest members promoted. Clamped at zero.
[float] meters. The distance that triggers promotion. Clamped at zero.
[enum NetwPredict.Pacing]. When the island's members open transitions.
[int] ticks. The input delay a [constant NetwPredict.PACING_DELAY_CLOSED] group holds. Clamped at zero.
[enum NetwPredict.Fidelity]. How this member is simulated. A member setting is addressed as [code](entity, member, param)[/code] through [method predict_island_set_member_param].
[Callable]. The substituted command producer for this member, or an empty callable for none.

32-bit float. Every [enum ColumnType] is passed to [method schema_add_column] and says what a value is stored as and how wide it travels. All of them but [constant COLUMN_VARIANT] are a fixed width, which is what makes a column a block of bytes and lets the session compute how many rows fit in a frame. Send anything of a length that varies through [method Netw.channel] instead.
64-bit float, for a value whose precision is the caller's to decide.
8-bit signed integer.
8-bit unsigned integer.
16-bit signed integer.
16-bit unsigned integer.
32-bit integer.
64-bit integer.
One bit on the wire.
[Vector2].
[Vector3].
[Vector4].
[Color].
[Quaternion], distinct from [constant COLUMN_VECTOR4] because smallest-three packing is a semantic rather than a width.
A route, the link one table draws to another. Resolve one back to a handle with [method entity_from_route].

The self-describing tier, what a [String] or a [Dictionary] compiles to. Legal in a schema and in a property set, rejected by [method table_create], because variable width has no memcpy and no rows-per-frame budget.

Counter. Frames addressed to a route this peer never saw issued. Two kinds of value share this enum. [method stats_get] takes any of them, and [method stats_snapshot] returns the same values under their lowercase names. A counter only ever rises and says how often something happened, so what matters is how fast it climbs. A gauge says how many there are right now and moves both ways. Every name carrying [code]drops[/code] or [code]skips[/code] counts something the session rejected on purpose, so a rising one points at a cause rather than being a fault itself.
Counter. Frames for a route that is lingering or a tombstone. Ordinary during a despawn, since frames already in flight have to land somewhere.
Counter. Frames for a live route whose node is gone.
Counter. Frames rejected because the receive backlog was already full.
Counter. Frames whose node path could not be walked.
Counter. Frames naming a component id the entity does not have.
Counter. Outbound frames with no route to send them on.
Counter. Outbound frames for an entity that stopped being live before the send.
Counter. Sync frames older than what has already been applied. Expected under reordering, and the reason stamps travel.
Gauge. Derived property sets currently registered.
Counter. Derived frames received.
Counter. Derived frames naming a set this peer has not compiled.
Counter. Derived frames from a peer not entitled to author them.
Counter. Derived frames whose schema hash disagrees with the local set. A rising count means the two builds compiled different declarations.
Counter. Per-recipient declared-set row frames sent.
Counter. Row frames that carried every column rather than a diff, which is what a peer gets before its baseline is established.
Counter. Row frames the installed encode stage rejected. A pass that sent nothing because its stage rejected everything otherwise reads exactly like a caught-up one.
Counter. Rows whose gather rejected, so no recipient was offered one.

Counter. Per-recipient retained row frames sent on the reliable lane. Rises only when a retained column changed for that recipient, so a flat count beside a rising [constant STAT_ROW_FRAMES_OUT] is the healthy reading rather than a stalled lane.
Counter. Windowed row frames sent, one per recipient per pass.
Counter. Ticks those frames carried in total. It exceeds [constant STAT_WINDOW_FRAMES_OUT] by the redundancy the window buys, so the two together read as the cost of healing without a retransmit.
Gauge. Sync property sets currently registered.
Counter. Full sync frames sent.
Counter. Full sync frames received.
Counter. Delta sync frames sent.
Counter. Delta sync frames received.
Counter. Sync frames naming a set this peer has not compiled.
Counter. Sync frames from a peer the set's [member NetwPropertySet.policy] does not admit.
Counter. Sync frames rejected because the stream's baseline is no longer trustworthy, so a delta cannot be applied against it.
Counter. Sync frames carrying a flag bit this build does not know.
Gauge. Entities armed for spawn but not yet sent.
Counter. Entities spawned out to peers.
Counter. Spawns received and materialized locally.
Counter. Packets handed to the carrier.
Counter. Bytes handed to the carrier, framing included.
Counter. Packets taken from the carrier.
Counter. Bytes taken from the carrier, framing included.
Counter. State acknowledgements sent, which is how a peer's delta baseline advances.
Counter. State acknowledgements received.
Counter. Acknowledgements sent on their own because no state frame was going out to carry them.
Gauge. Entities live but not yet fully brought up.
Gauge. Interest layers declared.
Gauge. Entities some layer is currently hiding from someone.
Gauge. Admitted entity-to-viewer pairs in the committed matrix. The closest thing to a cost of the current interest configuration.
Gauge. Entities awaiting the next recompute.
Gauge. Interest changes queued for relay.
Counter. Entity visibility changes committed. Rising fast means entities are flapping across a boundary, which costs a spawn or despawn each way.
Gauge. Entities declared for prediction on this peer.
Gauge. Entities keeping a rewind timeline.
Counter. Corrections applied. The headline prediction health number.
Gauge. The deepest replay queue seen, which bounds how far a correction had to rewind.
Counter. Transitions authority replayed.
Counter. Ticks whose input never arrived, resolved by the entity's [constant PREDICT_PARAM_MISSING_POLICY].
Gauge. Actions awaiting their acknowledgement.
Gauge. Predicted effects armed but not yet confirmed.
Number of times a prediction gate used its default because the declared path returned no value.
Gauge. Entities holding a display runtime.
Gauge. Entities with nothing left to interpolate toward. A persistent non-zero value means the buffer is too shallow for the current jitter.
Gauge. Entities whose display is idle because nothing is moving.
Gauge. Entities currently extrapolating under [constant TIMELINE_MODE_FORECAST].
Counter. Times a display jumped rather than smoothed.
Gauge. The largest gap seen between a display and the newest sample it has, in ticks.
Gauge. The furthest any forecast has been projected past its newest sample, in ticks. Compare against [constant DISPLAY_PARAM_MAX_FORECAST_TICKS].
Counter. Gate verdicts of [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST].
Counter. Gate verdicts of [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_SKIP].
Counter. Gate verdicts of [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAVAILABLE].
Counter. Refusals returned with [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNAUTHORIZED]. This is the one to watch, because it counts peers asking for what they are not entitled to.
Counter. Gate verdicts of [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_INVALID_DATA].
Counter. Gate verdicts of [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_BUSY].
Counter. Table frames naming a wire id this peer has no table for.
Counter. Table frames whose schema hash disagrees with the local declaration. A rising count means the two builds sealed different schemas, which a mid-session script reload is enough to cause.
Counter. Table frames carrying a flag bit this build does not implement.
Counter. Table frames whose routes or columns ran out of bytes.
Counter. Table frames from a peer that is not the authority.
Counter. Table frames older than what the table has already applied, beyond the decoder's reorder window. Expected under reordering, and the reason the tick rides every frame.
Counter. Rows naming a route this peer has tombstoned. The count a resurrection attempt would show up as.
Counter. Rows older than the row they would overwrite, or older than the removal that already took that route away.
Counter. Send-pump skips for a component whose node is no longer valid.
Counter. Send-pump skips for a node belonging to no entity.
Counter. Send-pump skips for an entity holding no wire route.
Counter. Send-pump skips where this peer is not the author. The ordinary reason a client sends nothing for somebody else's entity.
Counter. Send-pump skips where interest admitted the entity to nobody.
Counter. Dirty-set entries skipped because the entity was gone by the time the recompute reached it.
Counter. Replays a declared group ran together, one per tick whose floor moved rather than one per authoritative row that arrived.
Gauge. Members the last joint pass stepped, lingering ones included.
Counter. Cells a joint pass drove from a relayed command.
Counter. Cells a joint pass drove from a local predictor standing in for an author whose command never arrived.
Counter. Passes that found a basis older than the history that could replay it and snapped to the newest recorded state instead.
Gauge. Departed members still stepped because the group's replay horizon has not passed their departure.

Counter. Sent bytes attributed to a peer and a channel. With [constant STAT_ATTRIBUTION_FRAMING_OUT] this totals [constant STAT_SENT_BYTES], and [method attribution_snapshot] is the same bytes broken out by peer, channel and route.
Counter. Received frame payload bytes attributed to the peer that sent them. This sits below [constant STAT_RECEIVED_BYTES] by the envelope and datagram framing.
Counter. Frames attributed on the way out.
Counter. Frames attributed on the way in.
Counter. Bytes counted as sent that carry no frame, which is the standalone acknowledgement traffic.
Counter. Bytes of frames that were encoded and then never sent, because the peer went unreachable or the session dropped the run holding them. These were never counted in [constant STAT_SENT_BYTES].
No peer is connected and none is being sought.
A host or join is in flight and may still fail.
The session carries traffic.
Teardown is in flight, and no new traffic is admitted.
No session, so no role yet.
A remote peer holding no authority. Very little should test for this, because a listen-server host is also a player.
Server authority with no local player.
Server authority held by a peer that is also playing. Server authority means this or [constant ROLE_DEDICATED_SERVER].
The name collides and the join may be renamed around it, which is what a debug join asks for. The caller picks a name nobody holds and admits that instead.
The name collides and may not be altered, because it came from an authenticated identity. The join is rejected rather than renamed, so the roster never disagrees with the account behind it.
[method transport_create_peer] builds a server peer from its settings and ignores its address.
[method transport_create_peer] builds a client peer joining the address it was given.
